items.title: ArcRmlUI
items.text: ArcRmlUI lets you build game UI as documents written in HTML-like markup (RML) with real CSS-like styling (RCSS). A document reads its data from Unreal MVVM view models and calls their functions, and it takes mouse, keyboard and gamepad input through CommonUI and Enhanced Input.

items.title: What you can build
items.text:
• Documents and layers: screens that open and close on CommonUI layers.
  • Data binding and lists: fields, conditions and repeated rows from a view model.
  • Events: buttons and keys that call view model functions.
  • Components: reusable pieces of a document.
  • Focus areas and gamepad navigation, with input and gamepad setup.
  • Text fields and drag and drop.
  • Frames and tabs.
  • Themes and animations.
  • Localization.
  • World markers: UI that follows a point in the world.
  • Editor preview: see a document in the editor with sample data.
  • Validation: check documents and their bindings before you run the game.

items.title: Is it for you
items.text:
• Unreal Engine 5.8, Win64.
  • Opening a document and writing a view model work from Blueprint. Struct lists (FArcRmlStructList) and view model resolvers are C++ (Struct lists, Source: resolver).
  • You write the documents and style sheets in HTML and CSS syntax; the guide does not teach either. For what differs from a web page see Coming from HTML and CSS.
  • A document opens on a CommonUI layer of the local player's viewport. Documents open only through OpenDocument, not inside a Widget Blueprint: no UMG widget hosts a document. To show one, open it from C++ or Blueprint, or with ArcRml.Open (Quick start).

items.title: What you get
items.text: The ArcRmlUI plugin. The samples plugin and the demo plugin are available separately on GitHub.

items.title: Where to start
items.text:
1. Quick start: open and close a first document from C++ or Blueprint.
  2. Project setup: enable the plugin and add the settings a project needs.
  3. Working with documents: edit, save and see the change.
  4. Concepts: the terms the rest of the guide uses.
  5. Samples: the companion samples plugin, one small sample per feature, and how to run each one.
  6. Walkthrough: one screen of the demo game UI, read part by part.

items.text: Project setup lists them. Questions before you buy: FAQ.

items.title: Blueprint view models
items.text: A view model can be a Blueprint: no C++ is needed for the data, the functions a document calls, or the Blueprint that opens the document. The BlueprintViewModel sample (see Samples) is a counter built this way. What still needs C++ is a resolver and FArcRmlStructList rows (Data binding).

items.title: Create a view model Blueprint
items.text:
1. In the Content Browser choose Add > Blueprint Class. In the Pick Parent Class window open All Classes, search for MVVMViewModelBase and pick it. Name the asset, for example BP_MyVM.
  2. Add a variable for each value the document shows. In the variable's Details, turn Field Notify on.
  3. Add a function for each action the document calls, and set the variable inside it with the Set node of the Field Notify variable (SET w/ Broadcast).
  4. Compile and save. The class the document names is the asset path, a dot, and the asset name followed by _C. The asset Content/UI/BP_MyVM of the project has the asset path /Game/UI/BP_MyVM, so its class is /Game/UI/BP_MyVM.BP_MyVM_C; use it as the class of the <viewmodel> declaration. In a plugin the first part is the plugin's name, as in the sample below.

The sample below follows these steps.

items.title: The view model
items.text:
BP_SampleVM is a Blueprint whose parent class is MVVMViewModelBase. It has three variables with Field Notify on:

Variable Type Default Title String Blueprint view model Count Integer 0 Step Integer 2

Only Field Notify variables can be read from a document. A document updates only when the view model broadcasts the field: the Set node of a Field Notify variable does that (the node is titled SET w/ Broadcast).

The function Increment has no parameters. Build it in four nodes:

  1. Drag Count from the My Blueprint panel into the graph and choose Get.
  2. Do the same for Step.
  3. Add an integer add node (+) and connect Count and Step to its two inputs.
  4. Drag Count in again and choose Set; the node is titled SET w/ Broadcast. Connect the sum to its Count input, and the function's entry node to its execution input.

items.title: The document
Which Blueprint functions a document can call
items.text:
• The function is a function of the view model Blueprint, not pure and not const. A custom event cannot be called.
  • The argument count in call(...) must match the function's input count exactly. Return values and output parameters are dropped.
  • There is no property write from RML: to change a field, call a function that sets it.
  • A call on a preview model only logs (see Editor preview).

The View models and Events pages cover call in full.

items.title: Opening the document from a Blueprint
items.text:
BP_BlueprintViewModel_Open is a Blueprint Function Library. Its function Open has the input PlayerController and the output Document (an ArcRmlDocumentRef). The graph is:

  1. Make Arc Rml Document Ref with Path set to /ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/BlueprintViewModel/BlueprintViewModel.rml.
  2. Get ArcRmlViewportSubsystem, from the PlayerController.
  3. Open Document on that subsystem with the made reference.
  4. Branch on the returned bool: when true, return the reference as Document.

The document needs nothing else, because it creates its own model. The Quick start shows the same open from C++.

items.title: Run it
items.text:
Play in the map L_ArcRmlSamples, then type in the console:

ArcRmlSamples.OpenBP BlueprintViewModel

ArcRmlSamples.OpenBP calls the Open function of the sample's Blueprint Function Library. ArcRmlSamples.Close closes the document again.

You should see the title Blueprint view model, Count: 0 and Step: 2. Each press of Add step raises the count by 2.

items.title: Next
items.text: • Documents: how a document opens and closes, and what its head declares.

items.title: Components
items.text: A component is an .rml file whose root is <component>: markup you write once and import into a document with a <dc-import> element, with props for the values that differ and slots for the children the importer supplies. The component file lives in a content root, by convention under UI/Rml/ like a document. The Component sample imports one file, Card.rml, twice.

items.title: Define a component
Import a component
Props
items.text:
• name is the absolute package path of the component file, .rml optional. A name that does not start with / is a compile error, and no folder is searched.
  • A prop is an attribute of the import. A prop declared in camelCase is written in kebab-case: accent-color="#ff9933" sets accentColor. An attribute that names no prop is a compile error.
  • A prop value is static text (title="Static title") or one whole-value expression (title="{{ Title }}"); text and {{ }} cannot be mixed in one value. A bound value reads the fields of the model the import sits in, here Title of the view model.
  • The import must be inside a data-model. The component's own expressions and call('', ...) then use that model (the second import's Pressed {{ Count }} times and Press button above).
  • data-for, data-if, data-model and data-key on an import apply to the <div class="sc-host">, the wrapper element the plugin puts around each import, not to the component's content.

items.title: Slots
items.text:
Children of the import without a slot attribute go to the default slot, and a child with slot="footer" goes to the slot of that name. A named slot with no children renders nothing. A slot name the component does not declare is a compile error. In the sample, the second import puts a button in the footer, and the button's call('', 'Increment') runs on the document's view model:

Component/ArcRmlSamplesComponent.h
UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, FieldNotify, Category = "Samples")
FText Title = INVTEXT("Bound title");

UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, FieldNotify, Category = "Samples")
int32 Count = 0;

UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category = "Samples")
void Increment();

items.title: When components expand
items.text: Imports are expanded when the document is compiled, into its .rmlc file, the compiled copy the plugin runs (Concepts). A mistake in an import or a component, such as an unknown prop or slot name, is reported then (Validation), not while the game runs.

items.title: Run it
items.text: Play in the map L_ArcRmlSamples and type ArcRmlSamples.Open Component in the console (Samples).

items.title: Next
items.text: • Documents: the head, opening and closing.

items.title: Concepts
items.text: The terms the rest of the guide uses, in the order you meet them. Read it once before the feature pages, or come back when a term is unfamiliar. The Glossary defines each term in a sentence or two.

items.title: Documents and content roots
items.text: A document is an .rml file: HTML-like markup with a <head> and a <body>, styled by .rcss style sheets it links. Documents and sheets live in a content root, the Content folder of the project (/Game) or of a plugin in the project that can contain content (/MyPlugin), and code names them by package path, such as /Game/UI/Rml/Menu.rml. A document opens per local player, from C++, Blueprint or the console; the Quick start opens one, and Documents lists everything its head can declare.

items.title: Layers and input modes
items.text:
Each document opens on a layer, a UI.Layer.* gameplay tag from <meta name="layer"> (default UI.Layer.Game). The layers stack in the order of the Layer Order setting; Documents has the default order and the rules.

<meta name="input-mode"> decides who gets input while the document is open:

Value Input game (default) The game keeps the keys and the mouse; the document takes no keys. For HUDs and overlays. menu CommonUI menu input: the document takes keys, gamepad and mouse, the game gets none. all CommonUI input for both: the document and the game both take input.

A menu or all document needs the CommonUI input setup for Confirm and Back.

items.title: View models and sources
items.text:
A view model is an Unreal MVVM object (UMVVMViewModelBase, made in C++ or Blueprint) that holds the data and functions of a screen; a document reads its data and calls its functions. The head declares each model with <viewmodel>: its name, its class, and one source that says where the instance comes from:

Source Where the instance comes from Sample create The document makes its own when it opens. FieldBinding context The GameInstance MVVM view model collection, by context name. SourceContext resolver A C++ resolver class, configured by the declaration's other attributes. SourceResolver manual Nothing; game code assigns it with SetViewModel. SourceManual path An object property chain read from the player, such as GetOwningPlayer.SampleViewModel. SourcePath

settable lets game code replace the instance of any of these (sample SourceSettable), and preview="<file>.json" binds stand-in data for the editor (sample EditorPreview). View models has the rules per source.

items.title: Bindings
items.text:
data-model="<name>" on an element makes a model's fields readable inside it. Only Field Notify fields (see the Glossary) are exposed, and the document updates when the model broadcasts a change. A field shows with {{ Field }}, and attributes bind it to classes, styles, attributes and conditions, as in this excerpt of the FieldBinding sample:

FieldBinding.rml
        <p>Count: {{ Count }}</p>
        <p>Progress: {{ Progress | format(1) }}</p>
        <p>{{ Message | to_upper }}</p>
        <p data-if="bEven">The count is even.</p>
        <p data-if="!bEven">The count is odd.</p>
        <div class="fb-badge" data-class-fb-odd="!bEven">odd or even</div>

A document never writes a property; it calls a function that does. Data binding has the types, transforms and lists.

items.title: Events
items.text:
data-event-<event> runs an expression when the element receives the event. call('', 'Function', args...) calls a BlueprintCallable function of a model; the empty '' means the model of the element's data-model, callIf(condition, '', 'Function', args...) calls only when the condition holds, and stopPropagation() stops the event there. data-action is a document action handled by the plugin, not a view model call: close closes the document. Another excerpt of the same document:

FieldBinding.rml
            <button id="fb-add" class="fb-button" data-event-click="call('', 'Increment')">Add one</button>
            <button class="fb-button" data-action="close">Close</button>

See Events.

items.title: Components
items.text: A component is an .rml file whose root is <component>, with declared props and slots. A document imports it with <dc-import name="<package path>" prop="value">; props are static text or a bound {{ }} value, and the component's markup is expanded into the document when the document is compiled. See Components.

items.title: The update cycle
items.text: A change reaches the screen one update later: the plugin draws documents on its own thread, so a view model change shows in a later UI update, never inside the call that made it. A field set several times in one game frame arrives once, with its last value. call() and data-action run on the game thread's next tick, so what the function changes shows one update after the click.

items.title: Compiled files
items.text: The plugin runs compiled files, not the sources: each .rml compiles to an .rmlc and each .rcss to an .rcssc next to it. In the editor a document whose sources changed is compiled again when it loads; a packaged build ships only compiled files, with the images and fonts they use. The compiled files are rebuilt from the sources, so they need not be in source control. Validation compiles and checks documents without opening them.

items.title: RmlUi
items.text: ArcRmlUI lays out and draws documents with RmlUi, an open-source UI library with HTML-like markup and CSS-like styling. ArcRmlUI extends it to behave more like a browser. This guide and CSS support are the reference for what a document can do. RmlUi's own documentation describes the library this plugin is built on; where it differs, this guide is right. Documents reach the game through view models and data-* attributes, and code through the plugin's own API (C++ and Blueprint).

items.title: Converting an HTML page
items.text: A web page you already have is a good start for a screen, but it carries what RML cannot run: scripts, event attributes, web fonts, remote style sheets. The converter turns a .html file into an .rml document and .rcss style sheets inside a content root, drops what cannot run with a warning for each, and keeps the rest as written. It is a head start, not a finished screen: you edit the .rml afterwards. Coming from HTML and CSS lists what else differs from a browser.

items.title: Run it
items.text:
Content Browser. Right-click one folder under a content root and choose Convert HTML to RML... in the RML section. The entry shows for exactly one selected folder. A file dialog asks for the .html or .htm page. The output is named after the page and written into the folder you clicked. If an output file already exists, a dialog lists the files and asks whether to overwrite them. When it finishes, a notification shows the summary line, for example ArcRmlConvert: wrote 2 files, 0 errors, 5 warnings. The report, one entry per removal, is on the page Convert of the ArcRmlUI log in the Message Log window.

Commandlet. For a build machine or a script, with your own project (where UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe is):

UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe "<Project>.uproject" -run=ArcRmlConvert -Source="<file.html>" -Dest="<folder>" [-Name=<Name>] [-Overwrite] [-json="<file>"]
Argument Effect -Source= The HTML file, a disk path, full or relative to the folder the command runs from. -Dest= The folder to write into, a disk path like -Source, under the Content folder of the project or of a plugin. A package path such as /Game/UI fails with "not under a content root". -Name= The name of the .rml file. Default: the name of the HTML file. -Overwrite Overwrite existing output files. Without it, existing files fail the run and nothing is written. -json= Also writes the report as JSON, in the format of the validator.

The log lists each removal and ends with a summary line (with -json=, a wrote '<json>' line follows it). The exit code is 0, or 2 when there is an error; warnings do not fail the run.

items.title: What it writes
items.text:
• <Name>.rml: the document. The <title>, the attributes of <html> and <body>, and the body are kept. An element with no children is written self-closed, so a <br> comes out as <br/> with no message.
  • One .rcss file for each local style sheet the page links, with the extension changed to .rcss and the path relative to the HTML file kept. The sheet text is copied unchanged, except print rules. The <link> in the document points at it.
  • <Name>.rcss for the <style> blocks of the page (<Name>-2.rcss and on when a link sits between them).
  • A copy of each local file the page or its sheets point to, when it is a file type the cook ships (png, svg, ttf, otf) and lies inside the folder of the HTML file.

Classes, ids, style attributes and CSS rules are not rewritten. After writing, the converter runs the validator on the new files and adds its findings to the report.

items.title: An example
items.text:
The input is the Converter sample's Converter/Html/Page.html and page.css. The page holds what RML cannot take: a <meta charset>, two Google Fonts <link> tags, a <script>, an onclick and a <br>.

Converter/Html/Page.html
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html lang="en">
<head>
<meta charset="utf-8">
<title>Main menu</title>
<link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">
<link href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto&display=swap" rel="stylesheet">
<link rel="stylesheet" href="page.css">
<script>console.log('menu loaded');</script>
</head>
<body>
<div class="menu">
<h1>Main menu</h1>
<p>Pick an entry<br>or press Back to leave.</p>
<button class="entry" onclick="startGame()">Start</button>
<button class="entry">Options</button>
<button class="entry">Quit</button>
</div>
</body>
</html>

The converter wrote this document. page.css became page.rcss beside it (not in Html/), with the same text.

Converter/Page.rml
<rml lang="en">
<head>
    <title>Main menu</title>
    <link type="text/rcss" href="page.rcss"/>
</head>
<body>
<div class="menu">
<h1>Main menu</h1>
<p>Pick an entry<br/>or press Back to leave.</p>
<button class="entry">Start</button>
<button class="entry">Options</button>
<button class="entry">Quit</button>
</div>


</body>
</rml>

The log, with disk paths shortened to package paths:

/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Converter/Html/Page.html(4): warning removed-meta: removed <meta charset="utf-8">: RML reads only the ArcRmlUI <meta> names layer, input-mode, hide-lower, keep-alive, frame, input-mapping, input-mapping-priority, any-input
/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Converter/Html/Page.html(6): warning removed-link: removed <link rel="preconnect" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com">: RML loads only local style sheets; for a font, provide a .ttf/.otf under a content root and an @font-face
/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Converter/Html/Page.html(7): warning removed-link: removed <link rel="stylesheet" href="https://fonts.googleapis.com/css2?family=Roboto&display=swap">: RML loads no remote style sheets; for a font, provide a .ttf/.otf under a content root and an @font-face
/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Converter/Html/Page.html(9): warning removed-script: removed <script>: RML runs no scripts
/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Converter/Html/Page.html(15): warning removed-handler: removed 'onclick' on <button>: RML runs no inline handlers, and the attribute would make the element take pointer input
ArcRmlConvert: wrote '/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Converter/Page.rml'
ArcRmlConvert: wrote '/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Converter/page.rcss'
ArcRmlConvert: wrote 2 files, 0 errors, 5 warnings

The five warnings are the <meta>, the two <link> tags, the <script> and the onclick; the <br> raises none. The two files are the .rml and the .rcss. The family 'Arc Samples Sans' in page.rcss stays: the project declares it in a font sheet.

items.title: What it removes
items.text:
Each removal is a warning with the line of the HTML file.

In the page Message starts with <meta> whose name is not one of the ArcRmlUI names removed <meta ...>: RML reads only the ArcRmlUI <meta> names <link rel="stylesheet"> that is neither a local file nor a remote address removed <link rel="stylesheet" href=...>: RML loads style sheets only from files <link> that is not a style sheet (preconnect, icon) removed <link rel=... href=...>: RML loads only local style sheets <link rel="stylesheet"> with a remote address removed <link rel="stylesheet" href=...>: RML loads no remote style sheets <link> to a font, or to a known web font host the same, plus "provide a .ttf/.otf under a content root and an @font-face" <script> removed <script>: RML runs no scripts onclick and every other on* attribute removed 'onclick' on <button>: RML runs no inline handlers ... <iframe>, <video>, <audio>, <canvas>, <object>, <embed>, <noscript>, <template> removed <tag> and its content: RML has no such element <base> removed <base>: RML joins relative paths to the document's own path a data-* attribute that RmlUi or ArcRmlUI reads removed '<name>' on <tag>: RmlUi or ArcRmlUI reads this data attribute media="print" on a <link> or <style>, an @page rule, an @media print block ... RML never prints

A reference it cannot copy keeps its text and warns '<reference>' is not copied: ..., with the reason: the file does not exist, it lies outside the folder of the HTML file, it is remote, or the cook ships no such file type. An @import is not copied either (the message says it is not followed); link the sheet from the document instead.

items.title: After the conversion
items.text:
1. Read the warnings and fix each one: a font needs an @font-face in a font sheet, a click handler becomes a data-event-click on a view model (Events).
  2. Check the validator findings in the same report: CSS the engine drops is listed there, see CSS support.
  3. Edit the .rml: add the <meta> names the screen needs (Documents), view models and input. Open it in the game from the console (Open the console) with ArcRml.Open and its package path, or preview it, see Editor preview.

items.title: Data binding
items.text: A document shows view model fields and reacts to their changes. Use it to keep what the player sees in step with game data without writing update code. The page uses seven samples (see Samples): FieldBinding, Lists, StructList, NestedViewModel, Aliases, InnerRml and VirtualList.

items.title: Fields
items.text:
A document reads only Field Notify fields: a Blueprint visible property marked FieldNotify, or a const BlueprintCallable function that has only a return value. The document updates when the model broadcasts the field. In a Blueprint view model, turn Field Notify on in the variable's Details (Blueprint view models). In C++, UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE writes a field and broadcasts it; a plain assignment is not seen. A document never writes a field; it calls a function that does (Events).

The FieldBinding sample has one field of each simple type:

FieldBinding/ArcRmlSamplesFieldBinding.h
UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, FieldNotify, Category = "Samples")
int32 Count = 0;

UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, FieldNotify, Category = "Samples")
float Progress = 0.0f;

UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, FieldNotify, Category = "Samples")
bool bEven = true;

UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, FieldNotify, Category = "Samples")
FText Message = INVTEXT("Not clicked yet");

UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, FieldNotify, Category = "Samples")
FLinearColor Accent = FLinearColor(0.2f, 0.6f, 1.0f);

UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category = "Samples")
void Increment();
FieldBinding/ArcRmlSamplesFieldBinding.cpp
void UArcRmlSamplesFieldBindingViewModel::Increment()
{
    const FLinearColor Accents[] = {FLinearColor(0.2f, 0.6f, 1.0f), FLinearColor(1.0f, 0.55f, 0.1f), FLinearColor(0.3f, 0.85f, 0.4f)};

    const int32 NewCount = Count + 1;
    UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(Count, NewCount);
    UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(Progress, (NewCount % 11) / 10.0f);
    UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(bEven, NewCount % 2 == 0);
    UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(Message, FText::Format(INVTEXT("Clicked {0} times"), NewCount));
    UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(Accent, Accents[NewCount % UE_ARRAY_COUNT(Accents)]);
}

{{ Field }} prints a field. These attributes bind a field of the document's view model, or an expression, to an element. The FieldBinding sample uses data-if, data-class-*, data-style-*, data-attr-* and data-event-click; lists are in the Lists sample below.

Attribute Effect data-if="expr" The element is shown only while the expression is true. data-visible="expr" Sets visibility; the element keeps its layout. data-class-<name>="expr" Adds the class <name> while the expression is true. data-style-<property>="expr" Sets one style property from the expression. data-attr-<name>="expr" Sets an attribute from the expression. data-attrif-<name>="expr" Sets the attribute <name> to empty while the expression is true and removes it while it is false. The tab bar marks its current tab this way. data-for, data-key Repeat an element per row, see Lists. data-event-<event>="..." Run an expression on an event, see Events. FieldBinding.rml
<p>Count: {{ Count }}</p>
<p>Progress: {{ Progress | format(1) }}</p>
<p>{{ Message | to_upper }}</p>
<p data-if="bEven">The count is even.</p>
<p data-if="!bEven">The count is odd.</p>
<div class="fb-badge" data-class-fb-odd="!bEven">odd or even</div>
<div class="fb-bar"><div class="fb-fill" data-style-width="(Progress * 100) + '%'" data-style-background-color="Accent"></div></div>
<progress class="fb-progress" max="1" data-attr-value="Progress"></progress>

Expressions can read fields (bEven, Progress), combine with operators, and call transforms with |. Text is single-quoted. The whole language, every transform and what an error does: Expression reference.

items.title: Transforms
items.text:
value | name(arguments) changes a value on its way into the document. In the sample, Progress | format(1) prints one decimal and Message | to_upper upper-cases the text.

Every transform, with its arguments and what a wrong argument does, is in the Expression reference.

items.title: Types
items.text:
Field type In the document bool Boolean. Integer types Integer. float, double Number. Enum Its name as text. FString, FName, FText Text. FGameplayTag Its name as text. FGameplayTagContainer An array of names. FLinearColor, FColor Colour; data-style-background-color="Accent" in the sample. FSoftObjectPath, soft pointers, UTexture* Text asset:<path>. FArcRmlImageRef Its Path as text. A view model object A nested model, see Nested view models. TArray An array. Any other struct A struct with all its members, read by member name (r.Name). A Blueprint struct member is read by the name typed in the editor. FArcRmlStructList An array of its rows, see Struct lists. TMap, TSet, other objects Empty; a warning is logged once per field.

Nesting is read up to 16 levels deep.

items.title: Lists
items.text:
A TArray is a list. data-for="r, i : Items" makes one element per row; r is the row and i its index. data-key="r.Name" on the same element keeps a row's element across inserts and removals, matched by that value. The Lists sample:

Lists.rml
<div class="ls-row" data-for="r, i : Items" data-key="r.Name">
    <span class="ls-name">{{ i + 1 }}. {{ r.Name }}</span>
    <span>x{{ r.Quantity }}</span>
    <button class="ls-remove ls-button" data-event-click="call('', 'Remove', i)">Remove</button>
</div>
Lists/ArcRmlSamplesLists.h
USTRUCT(BlueprintType)
struct FArcRmlSamplesListsRow
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

    UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, Category = "Samples")
    FString Name;

    UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, Category = "Samples")
    int32 Quantity = 0;
};

UCLASS()
class UArcRmlSamplesListsViewModel : public UMVVMViewModelBase
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    UArcRmlSamplesListsViewModel();

    UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, FieldNotify, Category = "Samples")
    TArray<FArcRmlSamplesListsRow> Items;

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category = "Samples")
    void Add();

    UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category = "Samples")
    void Remove(int32 Index);

private:
    int32 NextNumber = 1;
};

A plain array sends its whole value when it changes, so announce the change with UE_MVVM_BROADCAST_FIELD_VALUE_CHANGED(Items) after you edit it:

Lists/ArcRmlSamplesLists.cpp
void UArcRmlSamplesListsViewModel::Add()
{
    FArcRmlSamplesListsRow Row;
    Row.Name = FString::Printf(TEXT("Item %d"), NextNumber);
    Row.Quantity = NextNumber;
    ++NextNumber;
    Items.Add(Row);
    UE_MVVM_BROADCAST_FIELD_VALUE_CHANGED(Items);
}

void UArcRmlSamplesListsViewModel::Remove(int32 Index)
{
    if (Items.IsValidIndex(Index))
    {
        Items.RemoveAt(Index);
        UE_MVVM_BROADCAST_FIELD_VALUE_CHANGED(Items);
    }
}

call('', 'Remove', i) passes the index as an argument; the function checks it before it uses it.

items.title: Struct lists
items.text:
A plain array sends everything on every change. For a long list that changes often, hold the rows in an FArcRmlStructList: it sends only the rows that were inserted, removed, moved or changed. Blueprint view models cannot use it. The StructList sample holds the same rows as Lists:

StructList/ArcRmlSamplesStructList.h
USTRUCT(BlueprintType)
struct FArcRmlSamplesStructListRow
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

    UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, Category = "Samples")
    FString Id;

    UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, Category = "Samples")
    FString Name;

    UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, Category = "Samples")
    int32 Quantity = 0;
};
StructList/ArcRmlSamplesStructList.cpp
UArcRmlSamplesStructListViewModel::UArcRmlSamplesStructListViewModel()
{
    Rows.SetRowType(FArcRmlSamplesStructListRow::StaticStruct());
    for (int32 Index = 0; Index < 3; ++Index)
    {
        AddRow();
    }
}

void UArcRmlSamplesStructListViewModel::AddRow()
{
    FArcRmlSamplesStructListRow Row;
    Row.Id = FString::Printf(TEXT("row-%d"), NextNumber);
    Row.Name = FString::Printf(TEXT("Item %d"), NextNumber);
    Row.Quantity = NextNumber;
    ++NextNumber;
    Rows.Set(Row.Id, Row);
}

void UArcRmlSamplesStructListViewModel::Bump(int32 Index)
{
    if (!Rows.GetKeys().IsValidIndex(Index))
    {
        return;
    }
    const FString Key = Rows.GetKeys()[Index];
    const FArcRmlSamplesStructListRow* Current = Rows.FindAs<FArcRmlSamplesStructListRow>(Key);
    if (Current)
    {
        FArcRmlSamplesStructListRow Row = *Current;
        ++Row.Quantity;
        Rows.Set(Key, Row);
        UE_MVVM_BROADCAST_FIELD_VALUE_CHANGED(Rows);
    }
}

void UArcRmlSamplesStructListViewModel::Reverse()
{
    TArray<FString> Order = Rows.GetKeys();
    Algo::Reverse(Order);
    Rows.SetOrder(Order);
    UE_MVVM_BROADCAST_FIELD_VALUE_CHANGED(Rows);
}
  • SetRowType names the row struct, and the constructor calls it before any row is set.
  • Set(Key, Row) adds the row or replaces the row with that key, Remove(Key) deletes it and SetOrder(Keys) sets the order; GetKeys() lists the keys in order and FindAs<Row>(Key) reads a row.
  • After a change the field is announced with UE_MVVM_BROADCAST_FIELD_VALUE_CHANGED(Rows).

The document reads the rows like an array. The key given to Set and the Id member are the same text here, so data-key="r.Id" matches:

StructList.rml
<div class="sl-row" data-for="r, i : Rows" data-key="r.Id">
    <span class="sl-name">{{ r.Name }}</span>
    <span>x{{ r.Quantity }}</span>
    <button class="sl-bump sl-button" data-event-click="call('', 'Bump', i)">+1</button>
    <button class="sl-remove sl-button" data-event-click="call('', 'Remove', i)">Remove</button>
</div>

items.title: Nested view models
items.text:
A field that holds a view model object, or an array of them, can be read through the parent's field name and called. Use it when each part is an object the game updates on its own and the document calls: a party with a leader and members, each its own view model. A struct array (above) holds plain data rows; a child announces its own changes and can be called. The NestedViewModel sample is that party: the leader is Child, the members are Children.

NestedViewModel/ArcRmlSamplesNestedViewModel.h
UCLASS()
class UArcRmlSamplesNestedParentViewModel : public UMVVMViewModelBase
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    UArcRmlSamplesNestedParentViewModel();

    UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, FieldNotify, Category = "Samples")
    TObjectPtr<UArcRmlSamplesNestedChildViewModel> Child;

    UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, FieldNotify, Category = "Samples")
    TArray<TObjectPtr<UArcRmlSamplesNestedChildViewModel>> Children;
};
NestedViewModel/ArcRmlSamplesNestedViewModel.cpp
UArcRmlSamplesNestedParentViewModel::UArcRmlSamplesNestedParentViewModel()
{
    Child = CreateDefaultSubobject<UArcRmlSamplesNestedChildViewModel>(TEXT("Child"));
    Child->Name = TEXT("Leader");

    const TCHAR* ChildNames[] = {TEXT("Archer"), TEXT("Healer"), TEXT("Scout")};
    for (const TCHAR* ChildName : ChildNames)
    {
        UArcRmlSamplesNestedChildViewModel* Member = CreateDefaultSubobject<UArcRmlSamplesNestedChildViewModel>(ChildName);
        Member->Name = ChildName;
        Children.Add(Member);
    }
}

The children are subobjects of the parent, made with CreateDefaultSubobject, so the create source makes the parent and its children together.

NestedViewModel.rml
<span class="nv-heading">Leader</span>
<div class="nv-row">
    <span class="nv-name">{{ Child.Name }}</span>
    <span id="nv-child-points">{{ Child.Points }} points</span>
</div>
<span class="nv-heading">Members</span>
<div class="nv-row" data-for="c : Children">
    <span class="nv-name">{{ c.Name }}</span>
    <span>{{ c.Points }} points</span>
</div>

{{ Child.Name }} reads a field of the leader, and c in data-for="c : Children" is one member. A leader or member announces its own changes and the document updates the value read through the parent. A call names the model it targets, see Events.

items.title: Aliases
items.text:
data-alias-<name>="Path" makes <name> stand for the field path Path on that element and everything inside it. Use it to shorten a long path you read many times. The Aliases sample shows the selected hero through sel:

Aliases.rml
<div class="al-card" data-alias-sel="Selected">
    <p id="al-name" class="al-name">{{ sel.Name }}</p>
    <p>{{ sel.Title }}, level {{ sel.Level }}</p>
</div>
<p id="al-long" class="al-result">Same name, written in full: {{ Selected.Name }}</p>
  • {{ sel.Name }} reads Selected.Name, so the two lines show the same text. When the "Next hero" button changes Selected, both lines update.
  • A model field with the same name as the alias wins over it, and the log warns that the alias is shadowed. Pick a name no field has.
  • In a component, the alias path must come from a prop whose value is a whole {{ path }}.

items.title: Inner RML
items.text:
{{ }} shows a string as text. data-rml="Banner" shows it as markup: it replaces the element's children with the string parsed as RML, again each time the string changes. The InnerRml sample shows one string from the game and one the player types:

InnerRml.rml
<p id="ir-banner" class="ir-line" data-rml="Banner"></p>
<!-- ... -->
<p id="ir-text" class="ir-line">{{ Typed }}</p>
<!-- ... -->
<p id="ir-rml" class="ir-line" data-rml="Typed"></p>

Banner is Welcome back, <span class="ir-gold">traveller</span>: the <span> becomes an element that the style sheet colours. Typed starts as <b>x</b>: {{ Typed }} shows those characters as they are, data-rml turns them into a <b> element holding x.

Never put player text in data-rml

Nothing is escaped in data-rml. A name, a chat line or a note a player typed can hold markup, and it becomes elements: a player can insert an <img> or a styled <span>. Show player text with {{ }} and use data-rml only for strings your own game or data wrote.

A localised text (loc) in data-rml is a compile error.

items.title: Virtual lists
items.text:
A list of thousands of rows needs only the rows near the visible part. data-virtual on a data-for element creates the elements for a window of entries and leaves the rest as data. The VirtualList sample shows 10 000 numbers:

VirtualList.rml
<div id="vl-list" class="vl-list">
    <button class="vl-row" data-for="n : Rows" data-virtual>Row {{ n }}</button>
</div>
VirtualList.rcss
.vl-list {
    height: 360px;
    overflow-y: auto;
    background-color: #1b212b;
    border-radius: 4px;
}

.vl-row {
    display: block;
    width: 100%;
    height: 36px;
    padding: 0 16px;
    text-align: left;
    background-color: #303846;
    border-bottom: 1px #1b212b;
}

Rows is a TArray<int32> that the view model fills with 1 to 10 000; {{ Rows.size }} is the entry count.

  • The parent of the data-for element is the scroll container. It needs a fixed height and overflow-y: auto or scroll. A parent that does not scroll vertically creates no rows, and the log shows the error Virtual data-for on <address>: its parent must scroll vertically.
  • Every row takes the size of the first row (its margin box). Rows of different heights, horizontal lists and other children in the scroll container are not supported.
  • The elements that exist are the visible rows plus one box height before and after. The scroll bar keeps the length of the whole list.
  • A row that leaves the window is removed, and with it its focus, hover and animations. When the rows are buttons, Up and Down move focus row by row and the box scrolls to keep the focused row in view.
  • data-key works as in Lists, but a key is read only for the rows in the window, so a repeated key outside it is not detected.
  • Two spacer elements before and after the rows give the scroll bar its length. They count as siblings, so :first-child, :nth-child, + and ~ on a row count them too. Style rows by class.
  • On a dc-import, put data-virtual on the host wrapper with data-for (Components).

items.title: Screen size, cursor and players
items.text: Use this page to know how big a CSS px is on a given screen, what mouse cursor a document shows and who hides or shows it, and what changes with more than one local player.

items.title: CSS pixels and screen pixels
items.text:
A px in an .rcss file is multiplied by the UE DPI scale of the game viewport before layout, so it is not one screen pixel in general. dp is multiplied the same way. Layout runs in screen pixels, in the content rect of the viewport (below).

The scale is the one UMG, Unreal's own widget UI, uses. It comes from Project Settings > Engine > User Interface > DPI Scaling: the DPI Curve and the DPI Scale Rule, times Application Scale. The plugin adds no Project Settings entry for it (Settings). With the default rule (shortest side) and curve:

Screen Shortest side Scale Room for a document 1920 x 1080 1080 1.0 1920 x 1080 px 3840 x 2160 2160 2.0 1920 x 1080 px 3440 x 1440 1440 1.33 1920 x 1080 px, a centred column

The curve is linear between its keys, so 1440p gives 1.33.

So a layout written for 1080p fills a 16:9 screen the same way at any resolution, at twice the pixels on 4K. The room is the content rect, not the whole screen: the platform's safe zone is removed from the screen, then the width is capped at MaxUIAspectRatio times the height, 16/9 by default, and the rect is centred. On the 3440 x 1440 screen the column is 2560 screen pixels wide, which is 1920 px; the document background still fills the whole screen.

Three settings change the size:

  • The aspect cap is not in Project Settings or Settings. A game changes it in C++ with UArcRmlUISettingsSubsystem::SetMaxUIAspectRatio on the game instance; 0 removes the limit. There is no Blueprint node for it.
  • To make every document larger or smaller, change the DPI Curve (or the rule) in that settings page, or set Application Scale.
  • For a UI size option in game, UArcRmlUISettingsSubsystem::SetUIScale (C++ only, on the game instance; no Blueprint node) sets Application Scale: it replaces the project value instead of multiplying it, and the project value comes back when the game instance ends.

When the window size or the scale changes, the open documents are laid out again.

items.title: Mouse cursor
items.text:
The cursor property is inherited. Over an element that takes the pointer, the document asks Slate for the cursor named by the cursor value under the pointer:

cursor Cursor pointer, hand Hand text Text edit beam move Cardinal cross ew-resize, col-resize Resize left-right ns-resize, row-resize Resize up-down not-allowed Slashed circle grab Grab hand grabbing Closed grab hand crosshair Crosshairs

Any other value, including default and auto, gives the default arrow. Over a part of the document that takes no pointer (empty space between elements) the document answers nothing, and the widgets below it and the game decide.

items.title: Who shows the cursor
items.text:
The plugin never sets bShowMouseCursor. CommonUI, Unreal's UI input framework, shows or hides the cursor from the input-mode of the topmost active document of each player (only that document pushes its config):

input-mode Cursor Mouse menu Shown Not captured by the game. The cursor stays shown while the document leaves. all Shown Not captured by the game. game (default) Hidden Captured by the game permanently. game, while a text field of the document wants keyboard focus Shown Not captured by the game.

CommonUI shows the cursor in capture mode too when the console variable CommonUI.AlwaysShowCursor is on, the viewport fakes touch from the mouse, or its virtual pointer is shown. The virtual pointer is CommonUI's on-screen pointer, which a gamepad accept clicks at; ArcRml.VirtualPointer 1 shows it (Console), and CommonUI also needs CommonUI.EnableVirtualPointer, a console variable that is on by default.

A game that wants a cursor over its HUD, with no menu open, opens a menu or all document or sets CommonUI.AlwaysShowCursor.

items.title: More than one local player
items.text:
Every local player has its own UArcRmlViewportSubsystem and its own layers and documents. Per player:

  • Layers: the layer root is created for the player's player controller and added to that player's screen. Each player has its own stack of documents.
  • Input: a document's input-mapping context is added to the Enhanced Input of the widget's owning local player, and its input mode goes to that player's CommonUI router.
  • View models: WorldContextObject of a function call is the player controller of the document's own player (Events).

Not per player:

  • The DPI scale: it comes from the whole viewport, so split-screen is not supported yet (Limits).
  • The console commands that act on a document, such as ArcRml.Open, act on the first local player only.

items.title: Documents
items.text: A document is an RML file (.rml) that describes one screen. Its <head> says where and how the screen opens: the layer it is drawn on, and whether the game, the document or both get input. Its <body> is what the player sees. This page lists everything the head can declare apart from view models (View models). It then shows how to open and close documents and explains layers.

items.title: The head
items.text:
The head of the GamepadMenu sample declares a layer, an input mode and an input mapping, links two style sheets and declares one view model. The excerpt ends at </head>; the <body> follows it in the file:

GamepadMenu.rml
<rml>
<head>
    <title>Gamepad menu</title>
    <meta name="layer" content="UI.Layer.Menu"/>
    <meta name="input-mode" content="menu"/>
    <meta name="input-mapping" content="/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/GamepadMenu/IMC_Sample_GamepadMenu"/>
    <link type="text/rcss" href="/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Shared/Samples.rcss"/>
    <link type="text/rcss" href="GamepadMenu.rcss"/>
    <viewmodel name="menu" class="/Script/ArcRmlUISamples.ArcRmlSamplesGamepadMenuViewModel" create="true"/>
</head>

Every <meta name="..." content="..."/> is optional, and each name is allowed once. An unknown name or a value not listed below is a head error: the document does not open (OpenDocument returns false) and the log names the line.

Meta Values Default Effect layer A UI.Layer.* gameplay tag that is in the Layer Order setting (Project Settings > Game > ArcRmlUI > Layers) UI.Layer.Game The layer the document opens on. input-mode game, menu, all game game leaves keys and mouse to the game, menu gives them to the document, all gives them to both (Concepts). hide-lower true, false true While the document is open, open documents on lower layers are hidden. keep-alive true, false false Closing parks the document instead of destroying it; opening it again keeps its scroll position, field text and other state (Keep-alive and preload). input-mapping The package path of an Input Mapping Context none The context's actions are bound as UI actions while the document is active, and their keys are readable as ArcKeys.<Action> (View models). Not allowed with input-mode game. input-mapping-priority An integer The Default Input Mapping Priority setting, 1 (Project Settings > Game > ArcRmlUI > Input) Priority of that context. Needs input-mapping. any-input true, false false Every key and pad press also sends an anyinput event to the document. true is not allowed with input-mode game. frame The package path of another document none Makes this document a tab of that frame document. A document with frame takes no other meta than input-mapping and input-mapping-priority.

items.title: Open and close
items.text:
Documents open per local player (more than one) through the UArcRmlViewportSubsystem local player subsystem. OpenDocument takes an FArcRmlDocumentRef, the document's package path, and returns whether it opened; CloseDocument with the same reference closes it.

C++Blueprint FirstScreen/ArcRmlSamplesFirstScreen.cpp
const FArcRmlDocumentRef Document{TEXT("/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/FirstScreen/FirstScreen.rml")};
return Viewport->OpenDocument(Document) ? Document : FArcRmlDocumentRef();

This is an excerpt: Viewport is the local player's UArcRmlViewportSubsystem. The Quick start has the whole function and the close call.

BP_FirstScreen_Open is a Blueprint Function Library. Its Open function (input PlayerController, output Document) runs Make Arc Rml Document Ref with Path /ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/FirstScreen/FirstScreen.rml, Arc Rml Viewport Subsystem (in the palette: Get ArcRmlViewportSubsystem) with the PlayerController input, Open Document on the subsystem and returns the document when Open Document returns true. Its Close function (inputs PlayerController, Document) runs Arc Rml Viewport Subsystem and Close Document.

How a call behaves:

  • OpenDocument returns false for an empty path, an unreadable head and while the player's world is being cleaned up. It returns true for a document that is already open.
  • An open or close requested while another one runs, for example from an Init function or an on-close call, is queued and runs after it, in request order. A queued open returns true.
  • The optional CloseAction is an Input Action whose keys also close the document in a menu or all document.
  • In C++ OpenDocument(Document, Init, CloseAction) takes an Init function that runs on each open, after the document's view models exist and before it is shown, so GetViewModel already returns them.
  • In Blueprint the async action OpenDocumentForPlayer has the same moment as its BeforeActivate pin, and AfterActivate fires once the open has succeeded.
  • CloseDocument takes an EArcRmlCloseReason, default Api.
  • PreloadDocument(Document) (also a Blueprint node) and DiscardDocument(Document) (C++ only) load a document before its first open and destroy its parked view: Keep-alive and preload.

A document also opens and closes without game code:

  • data-action="close" on an element closes the document, and data-action="open:<package path>" opens another one.
  • In a menu or all document the CommonUI Back action closes it when nothing in the document handles Back first (Events).
  • ArcRml.Open <Path> and ArcRml.Close <Path> in the console, for example ArcRml.Open /ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/FirstScreen/FirstScreen.rml.

Game code learns about documents from three events on the subsystem, assignable in Blueprint: OnDocumentActivated and OnDocumentDeactivated (they follow the CommonUI activation of the document, so opening a document on top deactivates the one below) and OnDocumentClosed with the document and its close reason:

  • Api: CloseDocument or ArcRml.Close.
  • Back: the Back action.
  • CloseKey: a key of the CloseAction.
  • DocumentAction: data-action="close".
  • Discard: DiscardDocument destroyed the document while it was closing.
  • Reload: the editor reloaded the document after a file changed.
  • WorldCleanup: the player's world was cleaned up.

items.title: Layers
items.text:
A layer is a UI.Layer.* gameplay tag. The Layer Order setting lists the layers from bottom to top, one layer per tag, and the default order is UI.Layer.Game, UI.Layer.GameMenu, UI.Layer.Menu, UI.Layer.Modal. A document on a higher layer is drawn over one on a lower layer, and Back and UI actions reach the topmost layer's activated document first. A dialog is a document on UI.Layer.Modal; there is no separate dialog flag.

hide-lower hides lower layers while a document is open: a UI.Layer.Menu document with the default hides a UI.Layer.Game HUD, and a dialog that should leave the menu visible behind it sets hide-lower to false.

Two functions of the subsystem, both Blueprint callable, read the stack: GetLayerDocuments(Layer) returns the open documents of a layer from bottom to top, and GetTopDocument(Layer) returns the last of them (empty when the layer has none). In C++, IsDocumentOpen(Document) tells whether one document is open; a document that is playing its leave transition counts as not open.

items.title: Drag and drop
items.text:
Use drag and drop for inventory-style screens where an item moves from one place to another and a slot decides what it accepts.

The DragDrop sample has three bag items you can drag with the mouse or carry with the keyboard or a gamepad, a hand slot that takes weapons, a ring slot that takes nothing from the bag, and a stash list that takes weapons and potions. Run it with ArcRmlSamples.Open DragDrop in the map L_ArcRmlSamples (Samples).

items.title: Run it
items.text:
Play in the map L_ArcRmlSamples and type ArcRmlSamples.Open DragDrop in the console.

What you should see:

  • Drag "Sword" onto the Hand slot with the mouse: a copy of the item follows the pointer, the slot turns green while it is under the pointer and shows Sword after the drop.
  • Drag "Potion" onto the Hand slot: the slot turns red and the drop does nothing. The Stash rows accept it.
  • The Ring slot turns red under every bag item and takes none of them.
  • With "Sword" focused, press F, move to a slot with the arrows and press Enter: the carry drops the item the same way.

items.title: Source and target
items.text:
A source is an element whose drag property is drag-drop or clone (clone: a copy follows the pointer; style it with :drag) and that has data-drag-type="<tokens>". Without data-drag-type the source gets dragstart and the drag is cancelled at once: no drag, no dragend. A target has data-drop-accept="<tokens>" and accepts a source that shares a token with it.

DragDrop.rcss
.dd-item {
    background-color: #3a4456;
    drag: clone;
}

.dd-item:drag {
    background-color: #2f6fb0;
    opacity: 0.8;
}
DragDrop.rml
<div id="dd-sword" class="dd-slot dd-item" autofocus="" data-drag-type="weapon" data-item="Sword">Sword</div>
<div id="dd-potion" class="dd-slot dd-item" data-drag-type="potion" data-item="Potion">Potion</div>
<div id="dd-hand" class="dd-slot dd-target" data-drop-accept="weapon" data-slot="Hand" data-event-dragdrop="call('', 'Dropped', 'drag:data-item', 'target:data-slot')">{{ Hand }}</div>
<div id="dd-ring" class="dd-slot dd-target" data-drop-accept="ring" data-slot="Ring" data-event-dragdrop="call('', 'Dropped', 'drag:data-item', 'target:data-slot')"></div>
<div id="dd-stash-0" class="dd-row dd-target" data-drop-accept="weapon potion" data-slot="Stash0" data-event-dragdrop="call('', 'Dropped', 'drag:data-item', 'target:data-slot')">{{ Stash0 }}</div>

The excerpt leaves out "Shield" and the Stash1 and Stash2 rows.

'drag:data-item' passes the dragged element's data-item value and 'target:data-slot' the target's data-slot. The call reaches the view model only when the nearest data-drop-accept ancestor of the element under the pointer accepts the source; a drop anywhere else, also on empty space, reaches no handler. The ring slot accepts no bag item, so a drop on it does nothing.

DragDrop/ArcRmlSamplesDragDrop.cpp
void UArcRmlSamplesDragDropViewModel::Dropped(const FString& Item, const FString& Target)
{
    if (Target == TEXT("Hand"))
    {
        UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(Hand, Item);
    }
    else if (Target == TEXT("Stash0"))
    {
        UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(Stash0, Item);
    }
}

The Stash1 and Stash2 branches are left out; they set their property the same way.

The core sets classes while a drag runs: drag-source on the dragged element, drop-over on an accepting target under the pointer, drop-invalid on a target that does not accept the source. The sample styles them in DragDrop.rcss.

items.title: Carrying with a gamepad or the keyboard
items.text:
data-drag-action="<UI action>" names a UI action of the document's input mapping context (Input and gamepad). On <body> it covers the whole document.

DragDrop.rml
<meta name="input-mapping" content="/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/DragDrop/IMC_Sample_DragDrop"/>
<body data-model="dd" data-drag-action="IA_Sample_Carry">

The sample maps IA_Sample_Carry to F and the gamepad's left face button. With a source focused, the action picks it up. While carrying:

  • arrows and the D-pad move focus, and drop-over / drop-invalid follow the focused element;
  • accept (Enter, Space, gamepad accept) on an accepting target drops it and runs the dragdrop call; on any other element it does nothing;
  • the action again does nothing; a mouse move or a primary press cancels the carry.

autofocus on "Sword" puts focus on the first item, so the first arrow or carry works at once. A source and its targets need tab-index: auto; nav: auto to take focus; the sample sets both on .dd-slot, .dd-row.

items.title: Back during a carry
items.text: Back plays the back sound if a style sheet declares one, then cancels the carry, returns focus to the source and ends there: the document stays open and no back event runs. A carry is the second step of the order of one Back.

items.title: The log lines
items.text:
A drag of a typed source logs in LogArcRmlUI at Log level, each line starting with ArcRmlUI:; <element> is the element's tag, id and classes. When a drag does not do what you expect, look for the line that matches:

  • Nothing happens when you press and drag: the source has no data-drag-type. It logs no drag line, only the error drag source '...' has no data-drag-type; the drag does not start, once per element (reported as a problem of the document in non-Shipping builds, an Error log line in Shipping).
  • The drag starts but the drop does nothing: drag target '<element>' accepted no is the target refusing the source, and drag cancel '<source>' reason the target does not accept the source ends a pointer drag released on such a target, or on an element with no data-drop-accept ancestor (empty space included).
  • drag cancel '<source>' reason ended without a drop: the drag ended with no element under the pointer.
  • drag cancel '<source>' reason back: Back cancelled the carry.
  • drag cancel '<source>' reason navigation focus ended: the document's keyboard and gamepad focus navigation ended during a carry.
  • drag action on '<element>' ignored, no drag-drop or clone source: the carry action fired on an element that is not a source.
  • drag place on '<element>' ignored, it is not an accepting target: accept was pressed during a carry on an element that is not an accepting target.
  • drag drop '<source>' -> '<target>': the drop on the target.

drag start '<element>' types '<types>' input pointer is a mouse drag and input nav a carry. drag target none is logged when the pointer leaves the current target.

Limits

  • Removing the source or one of its ancestors mid-drag (a data-if turning false), losing pointer capture or a new press cancels the drag: the clone goes and nothing is dropped.
  • The pointer capture belongs to the button that pressed first; another mouse button does not end the drag.

items.title: Editor preview
items.text: A document can declare a view model whose data is a JSON file. The data stands in for the real view model, so a designer sees real-looking values without code, in the editor and in a game.

items.title: The declaration and the JSON
When the data shows
items.text:
The data shows in the editor preview and in a game with a local player, when all of these hold:

  • The build is not a Shipping build.
  • The console variable ArcRml.PreviewHidden is 0. It applies to documents opened afterwards and does not exist in Shipping.
  • The JSON file exists.

Otherwise the model binds default values and its field ArcResolved is false. The sample shows a fallback line with it:

EditorPreview.rml
<p data-if="!ArcResolved">No preview data is shown.</p>

Never make live behaviour depend on preview data. A function called on a preview model only logs, so a button that calls one does nothing except log.

items.title: Open the preview tab
items.text:
In the Content Browser, double-click EditorPreview.rml: the preview tab opens and shows the sample with the base data, "Aldric, level 7", a health bar and three items. Its toolbar has Resolution, Variant (Base and the variants of the document's preview files), Theme, Background, Inspect, Open in text editor and Reload. Beside the view, the panels are Bindings, Diagnostics, Inspector and Input:

  • Bindings lists the document's view models; for a preview model it edits the JSON data: add keys, rename or remove them, and override a value in the selected variant.
  • Diagnostics lists the errors and warnings of the open document.
  • Inspector shows the elements you pick with Inspect: tree, box model and rules by selector (Debugging layout).
  • Input lists the actions of the document's input mapping context for keyboard or gamepad.

The Variant menu ends with Add variant..., which asks for a name and adds an empty variant to every JSON preview file of the document that lacks it. It is disabled when the document has no JSON preview file that loaded.

items.title: In a game
items.text:
In a running game, open the console and type:

ArcRml.Preview /ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/EditorPreview/EditorPreview.rml LowHealth

ArcRml.Preview <Path> [Variant] opens the document with a variant and reopens it when it is open. <Path> is the document's package path. Leave out the variant for the base data.

You should see the sample panel in the game with "Aldric, level 7", the line "Health is low." and the one item "Stone axe". ArcRml.Close /ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/EditorPreview/EditorPreview.rml or the sample's Close button closes it.

items.title: Events
items.text:
An element runs an expression when it receives an event. Use it to turn clicks, keys and Back into calls to your game. data-event-<event>="..." takes any RmlUi event name (list; click, mouseup, keydown, back, ...), and its expression is a list of calls separated by ;.

  • call(...) calls a function of a view model; callIf(...) calls it only while a condition is true.
  • An event bubbles: it runs the handlers of the element and then of its ancestors. stopPropagation() ends it at the element.
  • back and uiaction (UI action) are events too.
  • data-action="close" and data-action="open:<package path>" are handled by the plugin instead of as view model calls.

The Events sample shows each form; its view model has a LastEvent text that the calls write.

items.title: Calls
items.text:
call('<path>', '<Function>', args...) calls a function of a view model. The path '' is the model of the element's nearest data-model; a path such as 'Child' or 'Children[1]' names a view model held by that model (Nested view models). The function must be:

  • a BlueprintCallable UFUNCTION that is not const, not pure, not a network function and not a BlueprintNativeEvent or BlueprintImplementableEvent. Otherwise nothing is called, the log warns that the function "is not a callable event function", and the validator reports unknown-function.
  • called with exactly as many arguments as it has parameters. Otherwise nothing is called, the log warns that it "received N arguments but takes M", and the validator reports call-arity.

Its return value and out parameters are dropped. A call does not change a field itself; the function does, and the document updates when it broadcasts the field.

Events.rml
<button id="ev-red" class="ev-button" data-event-click="call('', 'Pick', 'Red', 1)">One red</button>
<button id="ev-blue" class="ev-button" data-event-click="call('', 'Pick', 'Blue', 3)">Three blue</button>
<button id="ev-caller" class="ev-button" data-event-click="call('', 'ShowCaller')">Who calls?</button>
Events/ArcRmlSamplesEvents.h
UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category = "Samples")
void Pick(const FString& Colour, int32 Amount);
Events/ArcRmlSamplesEvents.cpp
void UArcRmlSamplesEventsViewModel::Pick(const FString& Colour, int32 Amount)
{
    UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(LastEvent, FText::Format(INVTEXT("Picked {0} x {1}"), Amount, FText::FromString(Colour)));
}

Numeric parameters take numbers and numeric text, and bool, text, name and FText parameters convert. An object parameter takes 'vm:<path>', the path of a view model reachable from the element's model, as in call('', 'Select', 'vm:Children[1]'). 'target:data-x' passes the data-x attribute of the element that has the handler, as in call('', 'Choose', 'target:data-id').

items.title: Arguments from the element
items.text: An argument is an expression, so a call can pass what the element knows: the row and index of a data-for (call('', 'Remove', i) in Lists), a component prop (Components) and the values of the event, ev.<name>, such as ev.button of a mouse event and ev.key of a key event (callIf, Event reference).

items.title: callIf
items.text:
callIf(condition, '<path>', '<Function>', args...) calls only while the condition is true. A mouse event has ev.button, 0 for the left and 1 for the right button, and a key event has ev.key, the key's name as a browser reports it (ArrowUp, Enter, Escape, a letter in lower case):

Events.rml
<div id="ev-mouse" class="ev-box" data-event-mouseup="callIf(ev.button == 0, '', 'Pointer', 'left'); callIf(ev.button == 1, '', 'Pointer', 'right')">Click here with the left or the right mouse button.</div>
Events.rml
<div id="ev-keys" class="ev-box ev-focusable" autofocus="" data-event-keydown="callIf(ev.key == 'ArrowUp', '', 'Step', 1); callIf(ev.key == 'ArrowDown', '', 'Step', -1); stopPropagation(ev.key == 'ArrowUp' || ev.key == 'ArrowDown')">Value {{ Value }}: focus this box and press Up or Down.</div>

The second box takes keys only while it is focused. Its autofocus attribute focuses it when the document opens. A <button> is a navigation stop by default, but a <div> or <span> is not, so the sample's style sheet makes the box one:

Events.rcss
.ev-focusable {
    tab-index: auto;
    nav: auto;
}

items.title: stopPropagation
items.text:
An event bubbles from the element to its ancestors, and every ancestor with a handler for it runs. stopPropagation() ends that at the element; stopPropagation(condition) ends it only while the condition is true. In the keys box above, a stopped keydown also skips the document's own default for that key, so ArrowUp and ArrowDown do not move focus.

Some events cannot be stopped; the Stop column of the Event reference says which.

In the sample, a click on "Inner, stops" counts only the inner click, and a click on "Inner, bubbles" also reaches the outer element:

Events.rml
<div id="ev-outer" class="ev-box" data-event-click="call('', 'Outer')">
    <p>Outer clicks: {{ OuterCount }}, inner clicks: {{ InnerCount }}</p>
    <div class="ev-row">
        <button id="ev-inner-stop" class="ev-button" data-event-click="call('', 'Inner'); stopPropagation()">Inner, stops</button>
        <button id="ev-inner-bubble" class="ev-button" data-event-click="call('', 'Inner')">Inner, bubbles</button>
    </div>
</div>

items.title: The world context object
items.text:
A function parameter named WorldContextObject is not an argument: the call fills it with the controller of the local player, and the RML passes nothing for it. A view model function uses it to reach the player and the player's subsystems, such as UArcRmlViewportSubsystem.

The "Who calls?" button of the listing under Calls runs ShowCaller:

Events/ArcRmlSamplesEvents.h
UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category = "Samples", meta = (WorldContext = "WorldContextObject"))
void ShowCaller(UObject* WorldContextObject);
Events/ArcRmlSamplesEvents.cpp
void UArcRmlSamplesEventsViewModel::ShowCaller(UObject* WorldContextObject)
{
    const UWorld* World = WorldContextObject ? WorldContextObject->GetWorld() : nullptr;
    if (!World)
    {
        return;
    }
    UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(LastEvent, FText::Format(INVTEXT("Called by {0} at {1} s"), FText::FromString(WorldContextObject->GetName()), FMath::FloorToInt(World->GetTimeSeconds())));
}

items.title: Back
items.text:
In a document whose input mode is menu or all, a Back press (the Back action of the project's CommonUI input, see Project setup) runs the back event on the focused element and its ancestors. If no handler stops it, the document closes. In a child focus area, focus first returns to the parent area before the event reaches the elements above the area (Back and the parent area). data-event-back on <body> makes a document handle Back itself. In the sample, the first Back runs ArmBack and stops the event, so the document stays open, and the second Back is not stopped and closes it:

Events.rml
<body data-model="events" data-event-back="callIf(!bBackArmed, '', 'ArmBack'); stopPropagation(!bBackArmed)">
Events/ArcRmlSamplesEvents.cpp
void UArcRmlSamplesEventsViewModel::ArmBack()
{
    UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(bBackArmed, true);
    UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(LastEvent, INVTEXT("Back pressed: press it again to close"));
}

items.title: UI actions
items.text:
An action of the document's Input Mapping Context (Input and gamepad) is sent to the focused element as a uiaction event, or to <body> when nothing in the document is focused. data-event-uiaction reads it as ev.action, the action's name. The action counts as handled only when the handler stops propagation; call and callIf alone do not. The demo's loading screen runs ToggleDevBar for one action and stops only that one:

LoadingScreen.rml
data-event-uiaction="callIf(ev.action == 'IA_ArcDemo_DevBar', '', 'ToggleDevBar'); stopPropagation(ev.action == 'IA_ArcDemo_DevBar')"

Without the stopPropagation the function still runs, but the action is not consumed: it goes on to the document's data-drag-action, data-hotkey and data-hotkey-cycle elements, and is only logged ("has no handler") when none of them takes it. See Event reference.

<meta name="any-input" content="true"/> (Documents) sends an anyinput event on every key and pad press, with ev.key, ev.device and ev.action. The press keeps its normal route whatever the handler does.

items.title: Document actions
items.text: data-action="close" closes the document and data-action="open:<package path>" opens another one. They are handled by the plugin and are not view model calls (Documents).

items.title: Run it
items.text: Play in the map L_ArcRmlSamples and type ArcRmlSamples.Open Events in the console (Samples).
