items.title: FAQ
items.text: Short answers to what you may want to know before using ArcRmlUI. Each links to the page with the detail.

items.title: Which engine version and platforms?
items.text: Unreal Engine 5.8 and Win64. Other platforms are not supported yet. See Project setup.

items.title: Does it work with UMG? Can I mix it with my widgets?
items.text: A document is not a UMG widget and cannot sit inside a Widget Blueprint: documents open only through OpenDocument, on a CommonUI layer of the local player's viewport. Your own widgets stay in the game next to the documents. A document reads its data from UMG Viewmodel (MVVM) view models. See Documents and Designing a game's UI.

items.title: Does it need CommonUI?
items.text: Yes. The layers are CommonUI widget stacks, and a menu takes keys through CommonUI and Enhanced Input. The plugin enables both with itself. A document that only shows information needs less input setup. See Project setup.

items.title: Can I use it from Blueprint only?
items.text: Opening and closing a document and writing a view model work from Blueprint. Struct lists and view model resolvers are C++. The samples plugin has a C++ module, so a project that runs it must build C++. See Blueprint view models and Quick start.

items.title: Does it ship in a packaged (Shipping) build?
items.text: Yes. A packaged build ships the documents and style sheets compiled; Package Everything is on by default, or you list the folders to ship. The editor preview data, the inspector and most ArcRml.* console commands do not exist in a Shipping build. See Packaging and Console.

items.title: Does it support gamepad?
items.text: Yes: arrows and the D-pad move focus between the elements of a menu, Confirm is Enter, Space or the gamepad's accept button, and Back is CommonUI's back action. See Input and gamepad and Navigation.

items.title: Does it support split-screen?
items.text: Not yet, and it has not been run. What split-screen gets today is in Limits; see also local players.

items.title: Does it support localization?
items.text: Yes, for the whole text of an element: loc puts it into a String Table and the text follows the current culture. See Localization.

items.title: Can I use Tailwind CSS?
items.text: Yes, through Tailwind's own command-line tool, which writes one style sheet the document links. The plugin ships no Node and no Tailwind, and some CSS is not supported. See Tailwind CSS.

items.title: Can I reuse an HTML page?
items.text: As a start: the converter removes what RML cannot run. See Converting an HTML page and Coming from HTML and CSS.

items.title: Which third-party licences does it contain?
items.text: The plugin contains code from RmlUi, lunasvg, plutovg (partly derived from FreeType), Taffy, Chromium, Ladybird, itlib and robin_hood, and the WHATWG character entity table and HTML user-agent style sheet. Their licences ship with the plugin. Two layout features follow the design of Blitz (MIT).

items.title: Where do I report a problem?
items.text: Use the support link on the plugin's entry in Edit > Plugins. Say which document fails and include the LogArcRmlUI lines; see Troubleshooting.

items.title: What is it not?
items.text:
• No JavaScript: a <script> is a compile error and no on* handler runs (Coming from HTML and CSS).
  • Not a web browser: part of CSS is not supported (CSS support).
  • No accessibility support: nothing is exposed to a screen reader or the Slate accessibility system (Limits).
  • No bundled font (Project setup).

More: Limits, Troubleshooting.

items.title: Forms
items.text:
Use form controls when the player sets a flag, picks one of a few options, drags a value or chooses from a list, and a view model must see the choice.

The FormControls sample has a checkbox, a radio group, a range and a select. Each shows a model value and sends every change back; a readout under them shows what the view model holds. Most form markup and CSS from a web page works; see the limits below. Run the sample with ArcRmlSamples.Open FormControls in the console in the map L_ArcRmlSamples (Samples). Text fields have their own page: Text fields.

items.title: Show and write back
items.text:
A binding on a control only shows the model value. The control's change does not reach the view model by itself: a model variable is read-only, and a write from the control is refused without a warning. Send the change with an event handler that calls a view model function:

  • data-checked, data-value and data-attr-value set the control from the model.
  • data-event-input and data-event-change hear the user's change and call() a function that sets the field.

A value written by a binding fires no event.

The sample's view model has one field and one setter per control. This is the checkbox's pair (excerpt of ArcRmlSamplesFormControls.h; ClassName, Volume and Quality follow the same pattern). A Blueprint view model uses a variable and a function instead (Blueprint view models):

FormControls/ArcRmlSamplesFormControls.h
UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, FieldNotify, Category = "Samples")
bool bSubtitles = true;

UFUNCTION(BlueprintCallable, Category = "Samples")
void SetSubtitles(bool bValue);

items.title: Checkbox
Radio group
items.text:
FormControls.rml
<input id="fc-warrior" type="radio" name="class" value="warrior"
    data-checked="ClassName" data-event-change="call('', 'SetClassName', ev.value)"/> Warrior
<input id="fc-mage" type="radio" name="class" value="mage"
    data-checked="ClassName" data-event-change="call('', 'SetClassName', ev.value)"/> Mage
<input id="fc-rogue" type="radio" name="class" value="rogue"
    data-checked="ClassName" data-event-change="call('', 'SetClassName', ev.value)"/> Rogue
  • Radios with the same name are one group: checking one unchecks the others. A group is the radios inside the same <form>; radios outside every <form> form one group per document and do not mix with the radios of a form.
  • data-checked with a string checks the radio whose value equals the string. The same data-checked="ClassName" on each radio therefore selects the one that matches. An empty string checks none.
  • Picking an unchecked radio fires input and change on that radio only; the radios it unchecks and a radio that is already checked fire nothing. ev.value is the picked radio's value.

items.title: Range
items.text:
FormControls.rml
<input id="fc-volume" class="fc-range" type="range" min="0" max="100" step="5"
    data-value="Volume"
    data-event-input="call('', 'SetVolume', ev.value)"/>
  • data-value sets the slider. input fires for every change the user makes while dragging or stepping, change once at release and once per key step; both carry ev.value. Use data-event-input for a live readout and data-event-change to commit.
  • A value is clamped to min and max and snapped to step.
  • Gamepad and keyboard: the range is a focus stop. Left and Right step it (Up and Down for orientation="vertical"), Home and End jump to min and max. Up and Down on a horizontal range move focus, as anywhere else.

items.title: Select
Readout
items.text:
FormControls.rml
<p id="fc-readout" class="fc-result">Subtitles: {{ bSubtitles ? 'on' : 'off' }}, class: {{ ClassName }}, volume: {{ Volume }}, quality: {{ Quality }}</p>

The readout reads the view model, so it shows the value after the setter has run.

Limits

  • A control's change never writes to a model field; call a view model function (Limits).
  • A value, checked or selected set by a binding or an attribute fires no event.
  • A control draws Chrome's native look, without its hover, active, focus and disabled looks. To style a control yourself, set appearance: none and use your own CSS.
  • A <button> never submits a <form>; only an enabled <input type="submit"> inside the form does. The type and value of a button are plain attributes.

items.title: Run it
items.text:
Play in the map L_ArcRmlSamples, then type in the console:

ArcRmlSamples.Open FormControls

Click the checkbox, pick a radio, press Left or Right on the range, press Enter on the select, move with Up and Down, press Enter again to pick. ArcRmlSamples.Close closes it again.

You should see the readout Subtitles: on, class: warrior, volume: 50, quality: medium, and it changes with each control you use.

items.title: Frames and tabs
items.text:
Use a frame with tabs for a hub screen whose pages are separate documents shown one at a time in the same place.

The FrameTabs sample is a frame document with two buttons and an arc-embed box, and two tab documents, TabA and TabB, shown in the box one at a time. Each tab counts "Add one" presses, and the count is still there after you switch away and back. Run it with ArcRmlSamples.Open FrameTabs in the map L_ArcRmlSamples (Samples).

items.title: The frame and its tabs
items.text:
A tab names its frame in its head, the <head> block of its document (Documents). The frame holds one arc-embed element, the box the shown tab is drawn in.

TabA.rml
<meta name="frame" content="/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/FrameTabs/Frame.rml"/>
Frame.rml
<div class="ft-embed" arc-embed=""></div>
  • Opening a tab opens its frame when it is not open yet and shows the tab in the frame. Opening the frame by its own path shows the first listed tab.
  • A tab is drawn inside its frame, so the frame decides its layer and its input mode. A document with a frame meta takes no other <meta> than input-mapping and input-mapping-priority (Documents); another one is reported as an error.
  • The frame must give arc-embed a size; the sample sets height: 200px on .ft-embed in Frame.rcss.
  • A frame cannot have a frame.
  • In your own project, open a tab like any document (Open and close): the Open Document node or OpenDocument with the path of the tab opens its frame too. Close the frame, not a tab, with Close Document or CloseDocument.

items.title: Switching tabs
items.text:
Switching is an ordinary OpenDocument of the other tab. The frame's two buttons call the view model; ShowTab takes the WorldContextObject the call fills with the player controller (Events).

Frame.rml
<button id="ft-show-a" class="ft-tab" autofocus="" data-attrif-selected="Shown == 0" data-event-click="call('', 'ShowTab', 0)">Tab A</button>
<button id="ft-show-b" class="ft-tab" data-attrif-selected="Shown == 1" data-event-click="call('', 'ShowTab', 1)">Tab B</button>
FrameTabs/ArcRmlSamplesFrameTabs.cpp
void UArcRmlSamplesFrameTabsFrameViewModel::ShowTab(UObject* WorldContextObject, int32 Index)
{
    const APlayerController* Player = Cast<APlayerController>(WorldContextObject);
    const ULocalPlayer* LocalPlayer = Player ? Player->GetLocalPlayer() : nullptr;
    UArcRmlViewportSubsystem* Viewport = LocalPlayer ? LocalPlayer->GetSubsystem<UArcRmlViewportSubsystem>() : nullptr;
    if (!Viewport || Index < 0 || Index >= UE_ARRAY_COUNT(ArcRmlSamplesFrameTabs::Tabs))
    {
        return;
    }
    if (Viewport->OpenDocument(ArcRmlSamplesFrameTabs::Tabs[Index]))
    {
        UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(Shown, Index);
    }
}

The code above is an excerpt: Tabs is the array of the TabA and TabB document references in the same file, and Shown only drives the selected look of the buttons. ArcRmlSamplesFrameTabs::Open opens TabA and returns the frame, since the frame stays open while the tabs switch and is the document to close.

items.title: Tabs stay once visited
items.text: A tab you leave is hidden, not closed. Its view model, scroll, field text and data-if state stay until the frame closes; showing it again does not create it again, so Count keeps its value. Closing the frame drops every tab, and the next open starts at 0. A hidden tab is not open: IsDocumentOpen is false for it, and an open of it shows it.

items.title: Models and styles
items.text:
• The frame's model (frame) and the tabs' models (taba, tabb) have different names. A call() goes to the tab model with that name, else to the frame. A tab may not declare a name that a kept tab declares differently: it is not embedded and the log reports cannot open: view model 'x' is declared differently by the kept tab 'y'.
  • The two tabs use one view model class under two names, so each has its own count.
  • A tab may not declare a view model name its frame declares. The log says cannot open: view model 'x' is also declared by its frame 'y'.
  • A tab's input-mapping is an error when the frame's input-mode is game, or when the frame uses the same mapping: the tab still opens, but its mapping is not added.
  • A tab is isolated like a page in an <iframe>: it looks as the same document opened alone at the size of the box.
  • No frame rule matches inside a tab and no tab rule outside it. Inherited and custom properties start from their initial values at the tab.
  • So a tab links its own style sheets: each FrameTabs tab links Samples.rcss and its own Tab.rcss, and a :root or html rule in a tab sheet refers to the tab.

Limits

  • A data-if on the frame that rebuilds the arc-embed element drops the kept tabs and embeds the shown one again.

items.title: Coming from HTML and CSS
items.text: ArcRmlUI documents look like web pages: tags, classes, a style sheet, flexbox. They are not a browser. This page lists what changes for a web developer, section by section. Each section says what you do in HTML and what you do here.

items.title: The document
items.text:
Every tag must be closed, because the parser is an XML parser, not an HTML5 one:

  • Void tags are self-closed: <br/>, <img/>, <input/>. A bare <br> fails with "an element is not closed".
  • There is no DOCTYPE; leave it out.
  • Entities: <, >, &, ", numeric references and   in text work. ' and named entities such as © stay literal text.
  • A missing <body> becomes an empty one.

In HTML you write an .html file. Here the file is .rml, with a root <rml> or <html>. Only .rml and .rcss files load.

The head takes four things:

  • <title>: stored, shown nowhere.
  • <link type="text/rcss" href="page.rcss"/>: type and href are both required, rel is ignored, and the file must end in .rcss. <link rel="stylesheet" href="page.css"/> logs "Link tag requires type and href attributes".
  • <meta name="..." content="..."/>: only the eight names Documents lists, each once. charset, viewport and the like are errors.
  • <viewmodel>: the data a document reads, see View models.

An inline <style>, a <script>, <template>, <link type="text/template"> and <body template> are compile errors. Styles go in a linked .rcss file; the style attribute works.

The converter turns an HTML page into this. An example shows the Converter sample's page and its result. The changed lines: the <!DOCTYPE>, <meta charset>, the two font <link> tags, the <script> and the onclick are gone, <html> is <rml>, page.css is linked as page.rcss with type="text/rcss", and <br> is <br/>.

items.title: Paths and images
items.text: A path that starts with / is a package path, /<Mount>/UI/Rml/Shared/Samples.rcss, where <Mount> is Game or a plugin the project loads. Any other path is relative to the document. Images are png or svg files; the cook ships only svg, png, ttf and otf from a content root. An image can also come from a texture asset: src="asset:/Package/Path.Object" draws a Texture2D without virtual texture streaming (Images). No font ships with the plugin, and a web font link does not load: declare each font in a font sheet, see Project setup.

items.title: Elements that behave differently
items.text:
Every tag the table does not name is a generic element styled by the default style sheet; an unknown tag is inline.

Tag Difference from HTML input Types: text (default), password, radio, checkbox, range, submit, button, reset. number, email, date, file, color and search behave as text. hidden is display: none. button Never submits a form. form Does not navigate. Clicking an input type="submit" inside it fires a submit event carrying the named values. select, option No optgroup. Up and Down on a closed select move focus instead of changing the value. label Targets for, or else its first descendant control. progress max defaults to 1; direction takes top, right, bottom, left, clockwise and counter-clockwise; a fill child draws the bar. img src, plus rect (crop) and sprite. No alt, no srcset. a No href behaviour. Use data-action or data-event-click. textarea rows, cols, maxlength, wrap.

Not present: iframe, video, audio, canvas, links between pages, the DOM. <svg> works with a src file. Text fields and focus: Text fields, Navigation.

items.title: No JavaScript
items.text:
A <script> is a compile error and no on* handler runs. What replaces it:

  • Data: a view model (UMVVMViewModelBase, C++ or Blueprint) is declared in the head and read with data-* bindings. View models, Data binding.
  • Click handlers: data-event-click="call(...)" calls a view model function. Events.
  • Navigation: data-action="close" or data-action="open:<package path>" closes the document or opens another. Events.
  • Tabs and frames: Frames and tabs.

items.title: CSS
items.text:
Most of what a game UI uses works: the box model, position (static, relative, absolute, fixed), float, flexbox, grid, aspect-ratio, shadows, transforms, transitions and animations, var(), calc(), gradients, @media, @keyframes, @font-face, nesting, and the modern colour syntaxes. The full tables, with what is partial, are in CSS support.

The gaps a web developer meets first:

  • position: sticky, columns, writing-mode, clip-path, resize, scroll-snap-*, container-type do not exist.
  • :has(), :target, :visited, :valid and :invalid never match.
  • @layer and @container blocks apply their rules unconditionally, without layers and without the condition. Each one logs an "Unknown at-rule" warning, which is expected. @import is not followed: link each sheet from the document.
  • Units ex, ch and lh and the functions env() and hwb() are not supported.

Where the default style sheet differs from a browser:

  • The sheet follows Chrome's (body margin 8px, headings, lists, tables, 13.33px sans-serif controls), with one addition: input, select, textarea and button are arrow-key stops (nav: auto).
  • No font ships. A rule with no font-family uses the configured fallback family.

A declaration ArcRmlUI drops is reported as a warning, for example "Declaration 'resize: none;' is dropped: unknown property 'resize'." or "... is dropped: invalid value.". The warning shows in the log of every build that is not a Shipping build, and the validator reports the same text before you run the game. A malformed block drops the rest of its sheet.

items.title: Bring a page over
items.text:
• Converting an HTML page: the editor converts a .html file into .rml and .rcss, removing what cannot run. The Converter sample's input and output are in An example.
  • Tailwind CSS: build a utility-class sheet with the standalone CLI and link it. The sample is Tailwind/Tailwind.rml (an excerpt):
Tailwind/Tailwind.rml
<rml>
<head>

    <meta name="input-mode" content="menu"/>
    <link type="text/rcss" href="/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Shared/Samples.rcss"/>
    <link type="text/rcss" href="Tailwind.rcss"/>
</head>
<body>
    <div class="absolute top-20 left-20 w-[720px] rounded-xl bg-slate-800 p-8 shadow-lg">
        <h1 class="text-3xl font-bold text-sky-400">Tailwind in RML</h1>
        <p class="mt-2 text-slate-300">Every style on this screen comes from Tailwind utility classes.</p>
        <!-- ... a button row, a divide-y list and a grid-cols-3 block ... -->
    </div>
</body>
</rml>
