items.title: C++ and Blueprint reference
items.text: The C++ and Blueprint types a game uses to open documents and react to them. The page an entry links to has an example. In C++, add the module named for a type to your Build.cs (Project setup) and include its header.

items.title: The viewport subsystem
items.text:
The object a game talks to is UArcRmlViewportSubsystem (module ArcRmlUI, header Host/ArcRmlViewportSubsystem.h). Each local player has one. In C++ call LocalPlayer->GetSubsystem<UArcRmlViewportSubsystem>(); in a Blueprint place the Arc Rml Viewport Subsystem node (palette: Get ArcRmlViewportSubsystem) and connect its PlayerController input. A function marked (C++) has no Blueprint node. Documents describes how opens and closes queue.

Function What it does OpenDocument(Document, CloseAction) Opens the document on its layer; returns false for an empty path, an unreadable head (the document's <head>, where its layer, input mode and view models are declared) and while the player's world is being cleaned up. CloseAction is an optional Input Action whose keys also close the document. OpenDocument(Document, Init, CloseAction) (C++) The same, with an Init function that runs on every open that activates the document, after its view models exist and before it is shown. PreloadDocument(Document) Preloads the document: queues it to be loaded in the background before it is opened; asking again for the same path does nothing. CloseDocument(Document, Reason) Closes the document; Reason defaults to Api. DiscardDocument(Document) (C++) Destroys the parked view of a closed keep-alive document. IsDocumentOpen(Document) (C++) True while the document is open; a document playing its leave transition counts as not open. PostBack(Document) Sends Back to the document's view. Returns false when the document is not open, is leaving or hidden, or takes game input only (its input mode is game). See Events. SetViewModel(Document, ModelName, ViewModel) Assigns a view model to a live declaration of the document, by name; returns false when the document declares none of that name. See View models. SetViewModelByClass(Document, ViewModel) The same, choosing the declaration by the view model's class; returns false unless exactly one declaration takes it, one whose source is manual or that is settable. GetViewModel(Document, ModelName) The view model of the shown document with that name, or null. Pure. GetLayerDocuments(Layer) The open documents of a layer, bottom to top; a frame is listed by its own path. GetTopDocument(Layer) The last of those, or an empty reference. GetShownTab(Frame) The tab a frame shows, or an empty reference when the frame is not open. See Frames and tabs.

Three events, assignable in Blueprint, are described under Documents:

Event Parameters OnDocumentActivated Document OnDocumentDeactivated Document OnDocumentClosed Document, Reason (EArcRmlCloseReason)

items.title: Open a document from a Blueprint
items.text: The Open Document for Player node (C++ UArcRmlAsyncOpenDocument::OpenDocumentForPlayer, module ArcRmlUI, header Host/ArcRmlAsyncOpenDocument.h) opens a document for a player in a Blueprint. Its inputs are Owning Player (OwningPlayer, the player's player controller), Document and an optional Close Action. Its outputs are two execution pins, each with a Document pin: Before Activate fires at the Init moment above, and After Activate fires once the open has succeeded. See Documents and Blueprint view models.

items.title: Types
items.text: Type Module and header What it is FArcRmlDocumentRef ArcRmlUIData, ArcRmlDocumentRef.h A Blueprint struct with one Path string: the package path of a document. FArcRmlImageRef ArcRmlUIData, ArcRmlImageRef.h A Blueprint struct with one Path string: the package path of an image. A view model field of this type reads as its Path text in a document (Data binding). FArcRmlStructList ArcRmlUIData, ArcRmlStructList.h A keyed list of struct rows of one row type for a C++ view model, sending only the rows that changed. See Data binding. EArcRmlCloseReason ArcRmlUI, Host/ArcRmlCloseReason.h Why a document closed: Api, Back, CloseKey, DocumentAction, Discard, Reload, WorldCleanup. Passed to CloseDocument and delivered by OnDocumentClosed (Documents).

items.title: Clock
items.text: ArcRmlClock::Seconds() (C++, module ArcRmlUIData, header ArcRmlClock.h) returns the seconds since its first call as a double. Store it in a view model as a time stamp; the arcsince transform then gives the seconds from that stamp to now on the clock the document runs on. ArcRml.Clock stops the document's clock in builds that are not a Shipping build (Console reference); the value Seconds() returns keeps running.

items.title: Editor Python
items.text: unreal.ArcRmlStringSyncLibrary.sync_strings(package_paths) does what Sync Strings does in the Content Browser for the given document package paths and returns the errors as <path>(<line>): <message>, or <path>: <message> when there is no line. See Localization.

items.title: Attribute reference
items.text: Every attribute and head tag a document can use, grouped by where it goes. Each row names the value, what it does and the page that explains it. Names in angle brackets are filled in: data-class-<name> is data-class-active.

items.title: Head <meta>
items.text:
<meta name="..." content="..."/>, each name at most once. Details and defaults: Documents.

Name Value Effect layer a UI.Layer.* tag from the Layer Order setting The layer the document opens on; layers stack in the order of the Layer Order setting. input-mode game, menu, all Who gets input while the document is open: game the game only, menu the document, all both (input mode). hide-lower true, false Hides documents on lower layers while open. keep-alive true, false Closing parks the document instead of destroying it, and keeps its state (Keep-alive and preload). input-mapping package path of an Input Mapping Context Binds its actions as UI actions while the document is active. input-mapping-priority integer Priority of that context; needs input-mapping. any-input true, false Sends anyinput on every key and pad press (Events). frame package path of a document Makes this document a tab of that frame (Frames and tabs).

items.title: Head <viewmodel>
items.text:
Declares one view model. Details: View models.

Attribute Value Effect name text, unique in the document The name data-model uses. class script path of a UMVVMViewModelBase class The model's class. create, context, resolver, manual, path see View models The source of the instance, exactly one: create, the document makes it; context, it is looked up in the GameInstance's view model collection; resolver, a resolver class makes it; manual, game code assigns it; path, it is read through a chain of properties or getter functions that starts at the player controller, its pawn or the local player. settable true Game code may replace the instance. optional true Focus entering the document's focus areas does not wait for an unresolved model, which it does without this attribute. on-close function name A function without arguments, called on the model when the view closes or is parked. preview path of a JSON file A stand-in model for the editor preview; takes no class or source.

items.title: Binding
items.text:
An expression reads the nearest data-model. Details: Data binding.

Attribute Value Effect data-model a <viewmodel> name The model the element and its children read. data-if expression Present only while true. data-visible expression Sets visibility; the layout stays. data-for row, index : List One element per row (Lists). data-key a member of the row The row identity of a data-for element. data-virtual none On a data-for element, creates only the rows near the scrolled area; the parent must scroll vertically (Virtual lists). data-rml expression Replaces the element's content with the RML in the value; never use it for text a player typed (Inner RML). data-class-<name> expression Adds the class while true. data-style-<property> expression Sets one style property. data-attr-<name> expression Sets an attribute to the value. data-attrif-<name> expression Sets an empty attribute while true, removes it otherwise (Navigation). data-pulse-<class> expression Removes and adds the class again on each change of the value, so an animation restarts; the first value never pulses (Styling). data-value expression Sets the value attribute; a model variable is read-only (Text fields). data-checked expression A boolean sets checked; other values check the element when they equal its value (Forms). data-world expression giving "x y z" Places the element over a world point (World markers). data-alias-<name> a data path Makes <name> stand for that path in the element and its descendants (Aliases). data-event-<event> expression list Runs the calls on an event (Events, event reference). data-action close or open:<package path> Closes the document or opens another (Events).

items.title: Input and focus
items.text:
Details: Navigation, Input and gamepad.

Attribute Value Effect data-focus-area area name Makes the element a navigation area, a focus area. data-focus-primary empty Marks the primary area, the focus area that gets focus first when the document opens. data-focus-parent area name Where Back returns before it leaves the area. data-focus-exit selector The element clicked when Back leaves the area. data-focus-enter area name On an item: its click sends focus into that area. data-focus-down area name, or empty for the primary area Down enters that area. data-focus-contain empty Keeps navigation inside the area and the areas in it, for a popup. data-focus-owner empty Marks the container of a popup and its trigger for ev.related_in_owner on blur (Events). data-focus-active set by the plugin on <body>; do not write it The name of the area that holds focus, for CSS selectors. data-focus-request expression Each later non-empty change focuses the element (Focus requests). data-nav-left, -right, -up, -down selector In the area, the arrow clicks the first visible match instead of moving focus. data-hotkey UI action name Clicks the element when the action fires. data-hotkey-focus UI action name The same, only for the focused element and its ancestors (A hotkey on the focused row). data-hotkey-cycle two UI action names, previous and next On a container: steps through its focusable items. autofocus none The element a document or area focuses first.

items.title: Drag and drop
items.text:
Details: Drag and drop.

Attribute Value Effect data-drag-type words separated by spaces Required on a drag source. data-drop-accept words separated by spaces A target accepts a source that shares a word with its data-drag-type. data-drag-action UI action name The action that picks up the focused source with pad or keyboard.

items.title: Components, localization, frames
items.text: Name Where Effect <dc-import> body Places a component (Components). <prop> component Declares a property of the component. <slot>, slot component body, import child Where the import's children go; slot="x" picks the named slot. loc an element with plain text The text is the String Table entry of that key (Localization). loc-<prop> <dc-import> The same for a component property. arc-embed frame element The box the shown tab is drawn in (Frames and tabs).

items.title: Console reference
items.text: The ArcRml.* console commands and variables a project uses to open, preview and test its documents. Type them as Open the console describes. <Path> is a document's package path, such as /ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/FirstScreen/FirstScreen.rml. Commands that act on documents work on the first local player of the world they run in. The last column says where each exists: Every build, Not Shipping (every build except a Shipping build) or Editor (editor builds). Of the commands in the tables below, only ArcRml.Validate, ArcRml.DumpExpanded and ArcRml.LayoutDump need the editor.

items.title: Open and preview
items.text:
Command What it does Exists in ArcRml.Open <Path> Opens the document on its layer. Every build ArcRml.Close <Path> Closes the document. Every build ArcRml.Preview <Path> [Variant] Opens the document with its preview data, or a variant of it; reopens it when it is open. A Shipping build shows no preview data. See Editor preview. Every build ArcRml.PreviewSet <Path> [Variant] Switches the preview variant of an open document without reopening it; without a variant it shows the base data. Not Shipping ArcRml.PreviewHidden 0\|1 Variable, default 0. At 1 preview view models bind with ArcResolved false (the field every view model has, true once the model exists: Fields every model gets), as in a Shipping build; it applies to documents opened afterwards. See Editor preview. Not Shipping ArcRml.Discard <Path> Destroys the parked view of a closed keep-alive document, so its next open loads it again; a path that is not parked only logs. Every build ArcRml.MaxFrameRate <Hz> Variable, default 120. Upper bound on how often a view that is animating is rendered again. Every build

For example, with the game running, ArcRml.Open /ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/FirstScreen/FirstScreen.rml shows the FirstScreen sample, a panel with the title "Hello from ArcRmlUI" and one line of text, and ArcRml.Close with the same path removes it (Quick start). The text shows only when /ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Fonts/Fonts.rcss is in Font Sheets (Settings).

items.title: Validate and write out
items.text: Command What it does Exists in ArcRml.Validate <Path> [<Path> ...] Validates .rml and .rcss files, given as disk paths (files or folders) relative to the project folder, like the Content Browser entry Validate RML: ArcRml.Validate Content/UI/Rml/Menu.rml checks /Game/UI/Rml/Menu.rml. The result goes to the Validate page of the ArcRmlUI Message Log. See Validation. Editor ArcRml.DumpExpanded <Path> Writes the document after its components are expanded to Saved/ArcRml/<Path>. Editor ArcRml.LayoutDump <Path> [OutDir] After the next UI update of an open document, writes its layout (<Name>.layout.json) and its element tree as it is at that moment, as HTML (<Name>.html) to OutDir, default Saved/ArcRml/LayoutDump; a relative OutDir is inside that folder. Editor

items.title: Inspect and simulate input
items.text:
Command What it does Exists in ArcRml.Inspect [Path] Toggles the inspector for an open document: an overlay in the view on which you click an element to select it, and a panel at the right of the game viewport, with the mouse cursor shown. Without a path it closes the inspector. Not Shipping ArcRml.InspectDump <Path> [X Y] After the next update, logs the inspector snapshot of the selected element: tree path, source line, box model, styles by rule. With X Y (view pixels) it selects the element there first. Not Shipping ArcRml.InspectEdit <Path> <selector> <property> <value> Applies an inspector inline edit to the first element that matches the selector; it is applied again after the document is rebuilt until the inspector resets. Not Shipping ArcRml.Click <Path> <Selector> [Index] Sends a left click to the centre of the Index-th visible element (default 0) that matches Selector. Not Shipping ArcRml.UIAction <ActionName> Posts a UI action, named like its Input Action asset, to the topmost open document whose input mode is menu or all, as if one of its keys fired it. Not Shipping ArcRml.SimulateKey <KeyName> [Tap\|Pressed\|Released] [AnalogValue] [@X,Y] [repeat N] [hold Seconds] On the next frame sends the key through the platform message handler, as a device does. Tap (default) sends the press and, on a later frame, the release; Pressed and Released send one of them. repeat N sends N auto-repeat presses; hold Seconds holds a gamepad axis for that long; @X,Y puts a mouse key's cursor at those pixels from the viewport's top-left corner for this command. Not Shipping ArcRml.Clock <Seconds>\|live Stops time for the UI at that many seconds: animations, transitions, double-click detection, smooth scrolling, the text cursor blink and slider and scroll repeat stop advancing. live returns to real time. Set it before the first ArcRml.Open: a value below a time already used plays animations backwards. Not Shipping ArcRml.ClockAdvance <Seconds> Moves the stopped time forward by that many seconds, to step animations; use it after ArcRml.Clock <Seconds>. Not Shipping ArcRml.VirtualPointer 0\|1 Shows or hides the CommonUI virtual pointer of the first local player, so a gamepad accept is also sent as a click at the pointer. Not Shipping

These commands are not described here: the performance, memory and verification commands (ArcRml.Perf*, ArcRml.MemoryReport, ArcRml.*Verify), which measure the plugin itself (the ArcRml.*Verify commands exist in editor builds only, the others in every build except Shipping), ArcRml.PointerPin, which holds the mouse pointer still for measurement runs, and ArcRml.Reparent and ArcRml.Wrap, which edit the element tree of open documents (editor builds only).

items.title: CSS support
items.text:
What ArcRmlUI does with the CSS a web page uses. A document is drawn by RmlUi, a UI library, so its style sheets (.rcss files, written in RCSS) follow RmlUi's rules, not a browser's. The tables list what the plugin supports. For a walk through the differences by topic see Coming from HTML and CSS.

Status words in the tables:

  • supported: RmlUi lays out, paints or acts on the value.
  • partial: works for the values or forms the Notes list.
  • parsed, no effect: accepted without a warning, but nothing on screen changes.
  • RmlUi-only: not CSS, an extension RmlUi adds; the Notes say what it does.

A declaration the engine drops is logged as a warning, see Validation.

items.title: At-rules
items.text:
At-rule Handling Notes @media supported Features width, height, aspect-ratio, orientation, resolution, hover, any-hover, pointer, any-pointer, color, prefers-reduced-motion, prefers-color-scheme, prefers-contrast, prefers-reduced-transparency, forced-colors, update, scripting and the range syntax. Types all and screen. @keyframes, @font-face, @supports, @property supported @decorator RmlUi-only Defines a decorator. @spritesheet RmlUi-only @starting-style skipped silently The block is skipped. @layer a, b;, @charset, @namespace skipped silently @layer name { ... }, @container applied without the condition, warns The rules apply to every element, in the order written, with the warning "Unknown at-rule". Layers do not exist and a container query is never evaluated. @import not followed Warns; link each sheet from the document. Any other at-rule top level: applied without the condition, warns; inside a style rule: dropped, warns At top level the same as @layer blocks. Nested in a style rule it is dropped with "At-rule '@...' inside a style rule is dropped."

items.text:
Keyword Status inherit, initial, unset supported, also on shorthands !important supported revert, revert-layer not supported

For the open CSS gaps, see Limits.

items.title: Event reference
items.text:
The event names a data-event-<event> in a document can listen to, what each carries and whether it bubbles. How to write the expression is on Events. An event runs the handlers of the element and then its ancestors; a handler that calls stopPropagation() ends that on an event that can be stopped and does nothing on one that cannot; the tables say which. Stopping also cancels what the event would do by default (a stopped keydown does not move focus).

A parameter is read as ev.<name>.

items.title: Events from the plugin
items.text:
Each bubbles up from the element in the Sent on column. All except focusvisible can be stopped. A data-event-uiaction, data-event-back, data-event-navnotarget or data-event-anyinput on an element does not make the element take a mouse click or focus.

Event Sent on Sent when ev.* back The focused element. When only the document or <body> has focus, or focus is outside the document: the element of the active area, else <body>. The Back action runs in a document whose input mode is menu or all (Back). none uiaction The focused element, else <body>. A UI action, an action of the document's Input Mapping Context, fires. action, the action's name anyinput The focused element. When the document itself or nothing in it has focus: the first autofocus element, else <body>. A key or pad button is pressed in a document with any-input. key, the Unreal key name; device, keyboard or gamepad; action, the mapped action or empty navnotarget The focused element. An arrow finds no target in the focus area (Navigation). direction, area, target_area focusvisible The element that gets the focus ring. Keyboard or pad navigation puts the focus ring on an element that does not have it yet (the element gets the :focus-visible pseudo-class at the same time). none

What stopPropagation() does on each:

  • back: handles Back, so the document stays open.
  • uiaction: the action counts as handled only when propagation is stopped; call and callIf alone do not stop it.
  • anyinput: ends the event at this element, so ancestor handlers do not run; the press keeps its normal route either way.
  • navnotarget: cancels the move.
  • focusvisible: nothing; the event cannot be stopped.

items.title: Events from RmlUi
items.text:
The events of the document engine. stopPropagation() ends an event only where "Stop" says yes.

Event Bubbles Stop ev.* click, dblclick, mousedown, mouseup, mousemove, mouseover, mouseout yes yes mouse_x, mouse_y; button (0 left, 1 right) on click, dblclick, mousedown and mouseup; offset_x, offset_y (pointer in the target), current_x, current_y, current_width, current_height (in the handler's element); the modifiers ctrl_key, shift_key, alt_key, meta_key keydown, keyup yes yes key, the key as a browser names it (ArrowUp, Enter); key_identifier; the modifiers textinput yes yes text mousescroll yes yes wheel_delta_x, wheel_delta_y focus no no none blur no no related_in_owner: true when focus moves inside the element's data-focus-owner (Navigation) input, change yes no value; on a checkbox or radio also checked; on a textarea, input also linebreak dragdrop yes yes Sent, for a source whose drag is drag-drop or clone, on the drop target under the pointer; mouse_x, mouse_y, and the modifiers when the drop is a mouse release (not a carry drop). Pass 'drag:data-x' and 'target:data-x' to call (Drag and drop) dragstart, drag yes no dragstart on the source when a drag starts (the first pointer move after the press, or a pickup with data-drag-action); drag on the source right after it and on each later pointer move of a mouse drag. A source without data-drag-type gets dragstart only: the drag is cancelled, so no drag and no dragend follow. mouse_x, mouse_y; the modifiers on a mouse drag; 'drag:data-x' and 'target:data-x' work in call as on dragdrop dragover, dragout yes yes Only for a source whose drag is drag-drop or clone (a drag: drag source such as a <handle> gets dragstart, drag and dragend only). Sent to each element the drag enters or leaves: the element under the pointer, or the focused element during a carry, and its ancestors. dragout also goes to the drop target after dragdrop. Since both bubble, a handler on an ancestor also runs for its descendants. Parameters as on drag dragmove yes yes Only for a drag-drop or clone source. Sent on the element under the pointer at each pointer move of a mouse drag, and on the element focus moves to during a carry. Parameters as on drag dragend yes yes Sent on the source when a started drag ends, dropped or not: a release, a drop during a carry or a cancel. Parameters as on drag, except that the modifier keys are only on the dragend sent at a mouse release, not on a cancel or a carry drop handledrag yes no Sent by a <handle> element on each pointer move while it is dragged; handle_x, handle_y, the offset in pixels from where the drag started, clamped to the move and resize limits of the handle's targets scroll yes no Sent on an element each time its scroll offset changes, whatever moved it; none animationend, transitionend yes no Sent on the element when an animation or a transition ends, once per animated property; property, the property's name submit yes yes One parameter per named control of the enclosing <form>, named after the control and holding its value, plus one named after the pressed submit button (submit when it has no name) holding that button's value tabchange yes no tab_index, sent by a <tabset> load, show, resize, unload no no none. See Document events below the table. hide no no Not sent: a parked keep-alive document is hidden with display: none. Use show and unload

input fires per edit or value change the user makes; change when a text field loses focus, on Enter in a text input, at the release of a range, or when a checkbox, radio or select changes. A value written by a binding fires neither (Text fields).

items.title: Document events
items.text:
load, show, resize and unload are sent only to the document's root element. Put their data-event-* on the root tag of the file, <rml> (or <html>); one on <body> or inside it never receives them. A tab embedded in a frame gets none of them.

  • load: once after the document is built, before its first data update.
  • show: after load, and when a parked keep-alive document reopens.
  • resize: when the view's content area changes.
  • unload: when the view is destroyed.

items.title: Expression reference
items.text: The language of {{ }} in a document and of the binding attributes that take an expression: data-if, data-visible, data-class-*, data-style-*, data-attr-*, data-attrif-*, data-pulse-*, data-rml, data-value, data-checked, data-world and data-focus-request. A data-event-* holds statements made of the same expressions. data-for and data-alias-* take a path, not an expression.

items.title: Literals
items.text: Literal Form Number Digits with at most one . and an optional leading -: 3, 0.25, 5., -.5, -2; a number cannot start with . and has no exponent. Every number is a double. Text Single quotes: 'Red'. \' is a quote and \\ a backslash; any other backslash stays as it is. Boolean true, false.

items.title: Names and paths
items.text:
A name starts with a letter and goes on with letters, digits, _ and .. Player.Name reads a member, Items[0] or Items[i + 1] an element (the index is cut to a whole number), Items.size the length of an array. ev.<name> reads a parameter of the event in a data-event-* (event reference); a parameter the event does not carry is empty.

The first name of a path is looked up as a field of the view model, then as a data-alias-* or data-for name of the element or an ancestor, then as a field whose name differs only in case. When two fields match that way, a warning names both and the one used.

items.title: Operators
items.text:
From the strongest binding to the weakest. Operators of one row run left to right.

Differs from JavaScript

  • &&, || and the transform | share one level: a || b && c is (a || b) && c, and a && b | f is (a && b) | f. Use parentheses. Both sides of && and || are always evaluated.
  • - before a name is an error; - belongs to a number literal only. Write 0 - Count. There is no %.
  • == compares text when either side is text (Types and conversion).
Operators Meaning ( ), ! Grouping; ! negates the operand right after it, so !a == b is (!a) == b. *, / Multiply, divide. +, - Add or join text, subtract. ==, !=, <, <=, >, >= Compare. &&, \|\|, \| And, or, transform: one level. ? : Condition.
  • c ? x : y evaluates only the chosen branch. Each branch reaches as far as it can: c ? a : b | f is c ? a : (b | f), and x | f ? a : b is (x | f) ? a : b. a ? 'x' : b ? 'y' : 'z' chains.

items.title: Types and conversion
items.text: Where Rule + Joins text when either side is text, the other side converted; otherwise adds numbers. -, *, /, <, <=, >, >= Numbers. Text becomes the number it starts with, or 0 ('abc' is 0); true is 1. ==, != Compare text when either side is text, else numbers: Count == '3' is true when Count is 3. True or false (!, &&, \|\|, ? :, data-if, data-visible, data-class-*, callIf) A number is true when not 0. Text is true only when it is true or 1 in any case; other text, also a name like 'Bob', is false. An empty value is false. Printed as text A boolean prints 1 or 0, so bEven == 'true' is false. An integer field prints as it is. Any other number, also the result of an operator, prints with at most three decimals and no trailing zeros: 1 / 3 prints 0.333, Count + 1 prints 4 when Count is 3.

items.title: Transforms
items.text:
value | name(arguments) passes the value as the first argument; value | name needs no parentheses without further arguments. name(value, arguments) is the same call. A transform given the wrong arguments returns an empty value; the ones marked "logs" also write a warning.

Transform Result to_lower, to_upper The value as text, in lower or upper case. format(n), format(n, true) The number with n (0 to 32) digits after the point; true removes trailing zeros. A wrong argument count or precision logs a warning; a value that is not a number or a bad third argument gives an empty value silently. round The nearest whole number; halves round up. arcclamp(low, high) The number limited to the range. arcmin(other), arcmax(other) The smaller or the larger of the two numbers. arcnum, arcnum(d) The number with digit grouping and exactly d decimals (0 to 18, default 0), in the game's language, halves to even. Text is not a number here. Logs once. arcpct, arcpct(d) The value times 100 as a percent, in the game's language, otherwise as arcnum. Logs once. arctime Seconds, rounded up and at least 0, as mm:ss, or h:mm:ss from one hour. Logs once. arcplural('Key') The plural form of a String Table entry for the number (Localization). Logs once. arcsince Seconds from the value, a time taken with ArcRmlClock::Seconds() (C++, module ArcRmlUIData, header ArcRmlClock.h), to the moment the binding is evaluated.

items.title: Event statements
items.text:
A data-event-* holds statements separated by ;, run left to right. Each statement is a function call: call, callIf or stopPropagation (Events). A name without parentheses calls with no arguments: stopPropagation is stopPropagation(). Arguments are expressions, transforms included. The example is not from a sample: the line sits in a document inside an element whose data-model names a view model, the '' in call means that model, and SetVolume is a function of it:

<input type="range" data-event-change="call('', 'SetVolume', ev.value | arcclamp(0, 1))"/>

Name = expression parses but always fails when it runs: a document never writes a view model field. Any other function name fails the same way.

items.title: Errors
items.text:
What you see, and the cause.

What you see Cause and what happens The binding or handler does nothing. The validator reports Data expression '<expression>' does not parse: <message>. A syntax error. The document compile reports a data-expression diagnostic (Validation) in a build that is not a Shipping build; the ArcRmlValidate commandlet reports it as a warning. Documents load compiled, so the run time logs nothing: the binding or handler is not created, and the diagnostic is the only report. A Shipping build reports nothing. A log line Could not find variable name '<address>' in data model., with the whole address (Player.Name) An unknown name. The binding is not created. Log lines Error during execution. <message> and Failed to execute program with <n> instructions: with a dump of the program An unknown transform or event function, an assignment, or an index that is not a number. A binding keeps its last value; the statements after the failing one do not run. Nothing is logged; the value prints nothing and is false A transform given wrong arguments: the value is empty.

Messages from RmlUi appear in LogArcRmlUI, prefixed RmlUi:: RmlUi errors as errors, RmlUi warnings as warnings.

items.title: Settings reference
items.text:
Every property of the plugin's settings class, UArcRmlUISettings. Edit them in Project Settings > Game > ArcRmlUI (the category in the table is the group inside that page), or in Config/DefaultGame.ini under [/Script/ArcRmlUI.ArcRmlUISettings]. A property that is a list takes one +Name=... line per entry. Restart is yes when changing the property in Project Settings makes the editor ask you to restart it.

[/Script/ArcRmlUI.ArcRmlUISettings]
GenericFontFamilies=(("sans-serif", "Arc Samples Sans"))
FallbackFontFamily=Arc Samples Sans
+FontSheets=/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Fonts/Fonts.rcss

The example sets one generic family, a fallback family and one font sheet, which is the ArcRmlUISamples font that declares Arc Samples Sans. A map such as Generic Font Families is one parenthesised list of ("key", "value") pairs.

Fallback Font Family FallbackFontFamily Fonts empty yes The family text is drawn with when no style sets one. Font Sheets FontSheets Fonts empty yes The font sheets, by package path, one entry each. With none, no font is loaded and text draws nothing: the plugin ships no font, and a warning that starts "No font face defined" is logged. See Project setup. items.title: Key labels
items.text: A document shows the key of an action with {{ ArcKeys.<name> }} (Input and gamepad). The label of a key is its entry in Key Labels; a key without an entry shows the engine's short display name of the key. The default entries replace the arrow keys and the D-pad with arrow and triangle glyphs. The labels navigate, stepLeft and stepRight built from the same entries are described under Fields every model gets.

items.title: Release notes
items.text: Each entry is a plugin version, as the Plugins window shows it. The number after Version in a heading counts the plugin's releases.

items.title: 0.1 (Version 1)
items.text:
First release, for Unreal Engine 5.8 on Win64.

  • Documents in RML and RCSS, opened and closed on CommonUI layers (Documents).
  • Data binding to UMG Viewmodel view models, events and components (Data binding, Events, Components).
  • Keyboard, mouse and gamepad input, focus areas and navigation (Input and gamepad, Navigation).
  • Text fields, forms and drag and drop (Text fields, Forms, Drag and drop).
  • Frames and tabs, themes and animations, localization, world markers (Frames and tabs, Styling, Localization, World markers).
  • Tailwind CSS through the standalone tool (Tailwind CSS).
  • Editor preview, validation, the inspector and the HTML converter (Editor preview, Validation, Debugging layout, Converting an HTML page).

Limits of this release: Limits.

items.title: Samples
items.text: The companion plugin ArcRmlUISamples holds small samples, one feature each, every one in its own folder: the document, its style sheet, a README.md and, under Source/ArcRmlUISamples/<Sample>/, its C++ (BlueprintViewModel, Converter and EditorPreview have none). Run one to see a feature working, or copy its files into your project as a starting point. The guide's code blocks are copied from these files.

items.title: Install
items.text:
1. Copy the ArcRmlUISamples plugin folder into your project's Plugins folder; put it nowhere else, or its content is not found. The plugin has a C++ module (Win64), so the project must build C++.
  2. Add the samples' font sheet to the font settings, in Config/DefaultGame.ini: +FontSheets=/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Fonts/Fonts.rcss in [/Script/ArcRmlUI.ArcRmlUISettings].
  3. For the samples that take keys and the gamepad, the project needs the input setup; the plugin's /ArcRmlUISamples/Input/ assets provide one.
  4. Restart the editor.

items.title: Run a sample
items.text:
Play in the map L_ArcRmlSamples (/ArcRmlUISamples/Maps/), then type in the console:

ArcRmlSamples.Open FirstScreen
  • ArcRmlSamples.Open <Sample> runs the sample's C++ open function, the code its page quotes.
  • ArcRmlSamples.OpenBP <Sample> runs the Open function of the sample's Blueprint Function Library BP_<Sample>_Open, for the samples that have one.
  • ArcRmlSamples.Close closes the document the last open returned.
  • Converter has no open function: in the game ArcRml.Open /ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Converter/Page.rml.
  • EditorPreview has no open function: double-click EditorPreview.rml in the Content Browser, or in the game ArcRml.Preview /ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/EditorPreview/EditorPreview.rml.

These commands exist outside Shipping builds.

In the table below, "Open" in the last column is ArcRmlSamples.Open and "OpenBP" is ArcRmlSamples.OpenBP.

items.title: Packaging the samples
items.text: With Package Everything on (the default) a packaged build ships the samples' documents. With it off, add their folder to Paths to Package: +PathsToPackage=/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml in [/Script/ArcRmlUI.ArcRmlUISettings] of Config/DefaultGame.ini. Most samples open their documents from C++ by a path string, which the cook does not see.

items.title: Sounds
items.text: A style sheet can attach a sound to a click, to the pointer entering an element, to focus arriving by key or gamepad, and to the document's Back and close. The Sounds sample declares each one and counts clicks. Run it with ArcRmlSamples.Open Sounds in the map L_ArcRmlSamples (Samples).

items.title: The properties
items.text:
A sound is a MetaSound Source asset. To use your own, make one, right-click it in the Content Browser and choose Copy Object Path (in the References section of the menu). Put asset: in front of the copied path and quote it: /Game/Audio/MS_Click.MS_Click becomes "asset:/Game/Audio/MS_Click.MS_Click". The sample declares each property in a style sheet:

Sounds.rcss
body {
    --sound-back: "asset:/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Sounds/MS_Sample_Back.MS_Sample_Back";
    --sound-close: "asset:/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Sounds/MS_Sample_Back.MS_Sample_Back";
}

.sd-group {
    --sound-click: "asset:/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Sounds/MS_Sample_Click.MS_Sample_Click";
}

#sd-hover {
    --sound-hover: "asset:/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Sounds/MS_Sample_Click.MS_Sample_Click";
}

#sd-focus {
    --sound-focus: "asset:/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Sounds/MS_Sample_Click.MS_Sample_Click";
}
Property Declared on Plays --sound-click any element On a click from the mouse, gamepad accept or the keyboard. Once per click, from the clicked element or its nearest ancestor that declares it, so a parent's sound serves every button inside it. --sound-hover any element Once when the pointer enters the declaring element; nothing while it moves inside it. --sound-focus any element When the declaring element takes focus from a gamepad or the keyboard, including when a move enters its focus area. --sound-back body On a Back, the first step of Back, whether or not the Back then closes the document. --sound-close body When the document closes through data-action="close" or the close or toggle key. A Back that closes it plays only --sound-back.

A property is never inherited: a child does not take its parent's value. The click sound is the one that still reaches children, because the lookup runs from the clicked element up through its ancestors and the nearest one that declares --sound-click plays. Hover and focus play only on the element that declares them: a child of a declaring element does not play its parent's sound.

items.title: What you should see
items.text: In the Sounds sample, a click on any of the three buttons in the group plays the click sound and raises the Clicks count by one. Entering the Hover button with the pointer plays a sound once, and so does moving focus to the Focus button with an arrow key or the gamepad. Escape or gamepad back plays the back sound, and Close plays the close sound.

items.title: What stays silent
items.text:
• Only gamepad and keyboard focus plays --sound-focus. Focus from a mouse press is silent, and so is focus the plugin restores by itself: after the focused element disappears, onto a frame's selected tab, and back to a parent area after a Back (only the back sound plays).
  • A keep-alive document that is opened again focuses the element that takes focus on open and plays that element's --sound-focus each time (Documents).

items.title: The compile errors
items.text:
The document compile fails for a --sound-* declaration that:

  • is not a quoted literal "asset:/Package/Path.Object": an unquoted value, another prefix, or a var();
  • names an asset that does not exist;
  • names an asset that is not a MetaSound Source (the message names the class it found).

Limits

  • Declare sounds in a style sheet. An inline style="" declaration is read as a texture reference and fails to compile.
  • Only a MetaSound Source plays; a sound wave or a cue is a compile error.
  • Every property whose name starts with --sound- is read as a sound, so a custom property of your own must not use that prefix.

items.title: Styling
items.text:
Use custom properties to switch a screen between colour sets, and transitions and animations to fade it or draw the eye to a changed value.

Two samples show the style features a screen uses most. Themes switches colour sets with custom properties, and Animations fades a screen in and out and flashes a value when it changes. Run them with ArcRmlSamples.Open Themes and ArcRmlSamples.Open Animations in the map L_ArcRmlSamples (Samples).

items.title: Themes
items.text:
The colours are custom properties on :root. A class on body declares them again, and every element below the body reads the new values through var(), so no other rule changes.

Themes.rcss
:root {
    --panel: #2c3a52;
    --text: #e8e8e8;
    --accent: #2f6fb0;
    --button: #3a4456;
}

body.theme-dark {
    --panel: #0c0e14;
    --text: #b8c0d0;
    --accent: #7a4fd0;
    --button: #1c212c;
}
Themes.rml
<body data-model="themes" data-class-theme-dark="Theme == 'dark'" data-class-theme-contrast="Theme == 'contrast'">
Themes.rml
<button id="th-dark" class="th-button" data-event-click="call('', 'SetTheme', 'dark')">Dark</button>

SetTheme is a function of the sample's view model; the button's call runs it:

Themes/ArcRmlSamplesThemes.cpp
void UArcRmlSamplesThemesViewModel::SetTheme(const FString& Name)
{
    UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(Theme, Name);
}
  • data-class-theme-dark="Theme == 'dark'": the class is on while the expression is true. The default theme has no class.
  • data-class-theme-contrast="Theme == 'contrast'" does the same for the High contrast button, with body.theme-contrast declared in Themes.rcss.
  • var(--muted, #9aa6ba) uses #9aa6ba when --muted has no value; the sample gives it a value only in body.theme-contrast. A var() with no fallback and no value makes the property invalid, so it takes its inherited or initial value.
  • @property gives a custom property a type and an initial value; the sample does not use it.

items.title: Enter and leave
items.text:
The host puts the class enter on body when the document is shown and leave when it closes. A rule on body.enter or body.leave starts the animation.

Animations.rcss
body.enter {
    animation: an-enter 0.4s linear forwards;
}

body.leave {
    animation: an-leave 0.3s linear forwards;
}
  • The leave ends when the body's animation or transition ends, at the latest after Leave Timeout Seconds (default 0.5 s, Project Settings > Game > ArcRmlUI > Transitions); then the document is removed. A leave animation longer than that is cut off. forwards holds the last frame until the document goes.
  • To see why a leave ended early, run log LogArcRmlUI Verbose in the console (Open the console). The log then shows leave started (timeout <s> s) and leave finished by <reason> after <ms> ms.
  • @starting-style is not supported: its rules are dropped. Use a @keyframes animation on body.enter for an entrance.

items.title: Pulse
items.text:
data-pulse-<class>="Expr" adds the class to the element each time the value changes, so an animation that the class starts runs again.

Animations.rml
<p id="an-hits" class="an-hits" data-pulse-flash="Hits">Hits: {{ Hits }}</p>
Animations.rcss
.an-hits.flash {
    animation: an-flash 0.6s linear forwards;
}

Each change of Hits removes the class flash and adds it back in the same UI update, and the class stays until the next change. The <class> is the part of the attribute name after data-pulse-.

Limits

  • The first value never pulses, and several changes before one UI update give one pulse.
  • A view created in the update that changes the value (a data-if branch, a new row) does not pulse.
  • An unkeyed data-for row reads whichever item sits at its index, so an insert or a removal pulses it. Put pulses in keyed rows (Data binding).

items.title: Tailwind CSS
items.text: To style a screen with Tailwind CSS 4, download Tailwind's standalone tool, run it on your documents to write one style sheet, and link that sheet in each document's head like any other. The plugin ships no Node and no Tailwind. The Tailwind sample is a screen written with utility classes only.

items.title: Get the tool
items.text: Download the standalone CLI for your platform from the releases of the official tailwindlabs/tailwindcss repository on GitHub (for Windows, tailwindcss-windows-x64.exe). It is one file and needs no Node. Put it anywhere you can run it from and call it tailwindcss below.

items.title: The input file
items.text:
Create tailwind.css next to your document. It is copied from the Tailwind sample:

Tailwind/tailwind.css
/* Rebuild Tailwind.rcss: tailwindcss -i tailwind.css -o Tailwind.rcss */
@import "tailwindcss" source(none);
@source "./Tailwind.rml";

@theme {
    --font-sans: 'Arc Samples Sans';
    --font-mono: 'Arc Samples Sans';
}
  • source(none) turns off Tailwind's automatic scan of your folders, so only the files named by @source count.
  • @source names a .rml file whose classes Tailwind keeps. Add one @source line for each document that uses Tailwind classes.
  • @theme sets the two font families Tailwind's base styles use. No system font ships with a game, and a font-family that no @font-face in your font sheets declares is an error of the validator. Use the family your project loads; the sample uses Arc Samples Sans.

items.title: Build the sheet
items.text:
In the folder of tailwind.css:

tailwindcss -i tailwind.css -o Tailwind.rcss

Tailwind.rcss appears next to tailwind.css. To see the screen in the picture above, run ArcRmlSamples.Open Tailwind in the map L_ArcRmlSamples (Samples); the console is explained in Open the console.

Name the output .rcss: a <link> loads only .rcss files. Link it in the head of the document, after the sheet your project shares:

Tailwind/Tailwind.rml
<link type="text/rcss" href="/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/Shared/Samples.rcss"/>
<link type="text/rcss" href="Tailwind.rcss"/>

Run the command again after you change classes in the document, or add --watch=always to rebuild the sheet on each save.

items.title: Known differences
items.text:
What still differs from Chrome's layout:

  • A label that wraps an input or a select is narrower than in Chrome.
  • A modal's content sits a few pixels higher.
  • Form-state variants (disabled:, enabled:, checked:, required:, placeholder-shown:, read-only:, peer-checked:) do not all match Chrome.
  • :has() (has-*), container queries (@container, @md:), indent-*, zoom-* and open: are not supported; see CSS support.

For what RML does differently from a browser, see Coming from HTML and CSS and CSS support.

What to do about the rest:

What you see Why What to do Warnings in the validator and in the log. They come from Tailwind's base styles and its @layer wrappers: browser-specific pseudo-classes, properties and values RML does not know. None come from the classes the sample uses, and the page renders right. Expect them. Only a warning at the rule of a class you use matters: it drops the declaration it names, and the class's other declarations still apply. Check that property in CSS support. font-bold text is drawn regular. The plugin does not synthesize bold; a browser does. Ship a Bold face in your font sheet. A focused button shows no outline unless you style it. There is no browser default focus outline. Style focus: yourself, as the sample's buttons do with focus:ring-2.

items.title: Text fields
items.text:
Use <input> and <textarea> when the player types a name, a search or a note, and a view model must see the text.

The TextFields sample has an <input> and a <textarea> that show the text while it is typed and the text that was committed when the field was left. Text fields behave as in Chrome. Run it with ArcRmlSamples.Open TextFields in the console in the map L_ArcRmlSamples (Samples).

items.title: The document
Run it
items.text: Play in the map L_ArcRmlSamples and type ArcRmlSamples.Open TextFields in the console. Click the name field and type Ann. Live: follows every key and reads Ann; Committed: stays empty and Commits so far: reads 0. Press Enter: Committed: reads Ann and Commits so far: reads 1. Click the notes field, type a line and click the name field: Notes live: followed the typing, and now Notes committed: shows the text and Commits so far: reads 2.

items.title: Typing and focus
items.text:
A text field types (caret, text input active) from the moment it takes focus. Typing mode means the field takes keys as text. With a gamepad or the keyboard:

Input In a typing field On a focused field that is not typing Gamepad back Ends typing: change fires, the field keeps focus, the caret goes The document's Back (here it closes the screen) Gamepad accept, Enter Enter commits an <input>; in a <textarea> a line break Types again; no click, no change Esc Nothing happens to the text or focus; the document gets an ordinary keydown whose ev.key is Escape Back Arrows, D-pad Move the caret, at its ends move focus Move focus

After gamepad back the field is an ordinary focused control: the D-pad moves focus from it, and a second gamepad back is the screen's Back (Navigation). A mouse press, a printable key, Backspace or Del on it types again.

Limits

  • A gamepad press that starts focus navigation ends typing, as gamepad back does.
  • Left and Right at the start or end of the text move focus, and so do Up and Down on the first or last line.

items.title: Troubleshooting
items.text: Symptom, cause and fix for what stops a document from showing or reacting. Quoted text is part of the log line (most lines start ArcRmlUI:); the log category is LogArcRmlUI, see Where to look.

items.title: No text is drawn
items.text:
Cause: no loaded font matches the element's font-family, or none is set. The log has a warning that starts RmlUi: No font face defined.. It continues either Missing 'font-family' property, or with RmlUi's long message that says the specified font face has to be "successfully loaded" and names the family.

Fix: declare a font sheet and name its family in a style sheet (Project setup, Fonts). A font sheet that fails to load logs ArcRmlUI: font sheet '<path>' in the ArcRmlUI setting FontSheets does not exist (or is not a package path (package path), is unusable), and a face that fails logs failed to load font face.

items.title: The document does not open
items.text:
• OpenDocument returns false for an empty path, an unreadable head and while the world is cleaned up. Fix: pass the document's package path, check its <head>, and open it after the world is up (Documents).
  • A head error. The head is the part of the document between <head> and </head>. An unknown or repeated <meta>, or a value that is not allowed, is logged with the file and line as <file>(<line>): <meta name='input-mode'> needs 'game', 'menu' or 'all', got '<value>' (input mode). Fix: use a value from the head table of Documents; the validator reports the kind head.
  • The layer is wrong. Three cases:
  • <meta name='layer'> has unknown gameplay tag '<tag>': the tag does not exist.
  • layer '<tag>' is not in the ArcRmlUI settings LayerOrder: the tag exists but is not in Layer Order (Project setup, Layers).
  • ArcRmlUI: cannot open '<path>': the layer host has no layer '<layer>': the layer host has no widget layer for the tag.
  • ArcRmlUI: cannot open '<path>': a view of it already exists. The document has a view already; close it first.

items.title: Arrows or the pad do nothing
items.text:
Check in this order:

  1. The document's input-mode is menu or all. A game document takes no keys (Documents).
  2. Something has focus. With focus nowhere the first arrow moves nothing, so give the entry element autofocus (Navigation).
  3. The target takes focus. A <button> does; a div or span needs tab-index: auto; nav: auto. Without nav an arrow does nothing and sends no navnotarget (Limits).
  4. In a project with menus, the input setup exists.

items.title: Back does nothing, or closes too much
items.text:
• Back does nothing, and the log has ArcRmlUI: '<path>': no keys are mapped to the CommonUI Enhanced Input back action. The project's input data has no key on its Back action. Complete the input setup; the validator reports it as input-mapping.
  • Back closes the document although a data-event-back handler ran. A call never stops the event. Add stopPropagation() to the handler, or leave it and let a child area's data-focus-parent take the Back. The order is in Navigation.

items.title: A field does not update
items.text:
Cause: the document reads only Field Notify fields and redraws when the model broadcasts the change. A plain assignment in C++ is not seen, and neither is a Blueprint Set node that does not broadcast.

Fix: in C++ write the field with UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE. In a Blueprint view model, set the Field Notify variable with its Set node, which the editor titles SET w/ Broadcast (Data binding, Blueprint view models). data-value cannot write a value back (Limits).

items.title: A call does nothing
items.text:
Cause: call() runs nothing and logs a warning. The line about a 'vm:<path>' argument, the path of a view model (Events), is an error:

Log line Cause '<Function>' is not a callable event function on '<Class>' The function does not exist, or is not a callable BlueprintCallable UFUNCTION that is non-const, not pure, not a network function and not a BlueprintNativeEvent or BlueprintImplementableEvent (Events). '<Function>' received N arguments but takes M The argument count differs from the parameter count. '<Function>' argument '<value>' does not convert to parameter '<name>' The value does not convert to the parameter's type. '<Function>' object parameter '<name>' takes a 'vm:<path>' argument An object parameter needs 'vm:<path>'. call('<path>', '<Function>') targets unknown view model The child path names no view model of the element's model. call('<path>', '<Function>') on '<model>' has no live view model The model is not set yet.

The validator reports a missing function as unknown-function and a wrong count as call-arity (Validation). A click on a data-action under a <body> without data-model logs action '<action>' was clicked under a <body> or embedded document root that has no data-model.

Fix: make the name, the argument count and the argument values match the function in the view model class, and give the <body> a data-model.

items.title: A binding shows defaults
items.text:
Cause: a view model that is not resolved still binds, from its class defaults, and its ArcResolved is false. This is the case before the first SetViewModel, the call that assigns a view model to a declaration, and for a preview model in a Shipping build or with ArcRml.PreviewHidden 1 (Editor preview).

Fix: for a manual model, call SetViewModel before you expect values; test ArcResolved in the document to show a fallback.

items.title: A hotkey does nothing
items.text:
• With the same data-hotkey on several elements, the click goes to the focused element or its nearest ancestor that has it; else to the first visible one in document order in the focused area, then in the document (an embedded tab's wrapper first). Another duplicate never fires, and there is no diagnostic. Fix: use each hotkey on one element (Navigation).
  • The log has ArcRmlUI: '<path>' input mapping '<mapping>' does not load as an Input Mapping Context (an error). The document opens, but its UI actions are unbound. Fix the path of the input-mapping meta.
  • A UI action that nothing handles logs UI action '<action>' has no handler, hotkey or cycle at the Log level. Fix: add a data-hotkey or a handler for it.
  • A data-event-uiaction handler consumes the action only if it also calls stopPropagation(); otherwise the hotkey runs as well.
  • The action must be in the document's input-mapping context, and the document needs an input-mode other than game (Input and gamepad).

items.title: A document is missing in a packaged build
items.text:
Cause: with Package Everything on, every document of every content root ships. With it off, a document that is neither in Paths to Package nor reached from a shipped document by a frame, a literal open: target or a reference of a Blueprint or data asset is not packaged (Project setup, Packaging). A data-action built from data (data-attr-data-action, data-attrif-data-action or {{ }}) is not followed; the cook logs '<document>' builds a data-action from data as a warning.

Fix: add the target to Paths to Package.

items.title: Where to look
items.text:
• The log category LogArcRmlUI; a diagnostic line is <file>(<line>): <message>. Warnings and errors outside Shipping also show in a bar over the viewport.
  • The editor's Message Log, the ArcRmlUI log pages, and the preview's Diagnostics panel (Working with documents).
  • The validator: it finds most of the above before the document opens.
  • The inspector: for an element with the wrong size or a style that does not apply, it shows the box model and the rules that reach the element, with their file and line.

items.title: Validation
items.text: The validator compiles RML documents and RCSS style sheets and checks them against the project: view model classes, fields and functions, images, fonts, localization keys and input mappings. It finds in the editor what would otherwise show up as a log line when a document opens. A run needs the editor.

items.title: Run it
items.text:
Content Browser. Select documents, style sheets or folders, and choose Validate RML in the context menu. A notification shows the summary line, ArcRmlValidate: N files, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Its Show Message Log link (a button when the run has errors) opens the Message Log window on the page Validate of the ArcRmlUI log. A run without problems has only the summary line on that page; every other line is a diagnostic.

Console. In the editor, open the console and type:

ArcRml.Validate <Path> [<Path> ...]

A path is a file or a folder on disk, relative to the project folder, and must be under a content root. The result goes to the same Message Log page.

Commandlet. For a build machine. UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe is in the Engine/Binaries/Win64 folder of your Unreal Engine install:

UnrealEditor-Cmd.exe "<Project>.uproject" -run=ArcRmlValidate -Paths="<Path>;<Path>" -WarningsAsErrors -json="<File>"
Argument Effect -Paths= Disk paths separated by ;, relative to the folder you run the command from, not the project folder. Without it the whole tree of every content root is validated. A path under no content root fails the run. -WarningsAsErrors A warning also fails the run. -json="<File>" Also writes the result as JSON: a summary of files, errors and warnings, the roots, and per diagnostic file, line, severity, code and message.

Each diagnostic prints as <file>(<line>): <severity> <kind>: <message>, followed by a summary line ArcRmlValidate: N files, N errors, N warnings. For example:

C:/MyProject/Content/UI/Rml/Menu.rml(12): error unknown-field: 'Helth' on model 'player' reads 'Helth', which 'PlayerViewModel' does not have

The exit code is 0, or 2 when there is an error, a warning with -WarningsAsErrors, a path under no content root, or a check that did not run.

items.title: What it reports
items.text:
Every diagnostic has a severity (error or warning) and a kind. The kinds a project meets most:

Kind Meaning unknown-field A binding reads a field the declared view model does not have. unknown-function, call-arity call() names a function the model does not have, or passes the wrong number of arguments. view-model-path A path source cannot work; see below. unknown-class, view-model-create A <viewmodel class> does not load, or is abstract and cannot be created. unknown-resolver, unknown-resolver-property A resolver class is unknown, or an attribute names no property of it. head A <meta> or <viewmodel> in <head> is invalid. input-mapping An input-mapping does not load as an Input Mapping Context, or a menu document has no key on the Back action. missing-image, missing-font, unknown-font-family An image or font file is not found under a content root, or a font family has no @font-face. missing-document An open: target is not an RML document. missing-loc-key A localization key has no entry in its string table. structural-conflict For example data-if and data-for on one element, or data-action without a data-model on <body>. undefined-variable, duplicate-id An RCSS variable is used and never defined; two elements share an id. component A dc-import component problem. data-expression A data expression does not parse (warning).

Other kinds come from the RCSS and RML compile (unknown property, invalid value, invalid selector, XML syntax, and similar), and from converting HTML into RML. A CSS declaration the engine drops is one of them, with the warning "unknown property" or "invalid value"; CSS support lists what is dropped.

items.title: view-model-path
items.text:
A path source reads the view model through a chain of properties, such as GetOwningPlayer.SampleViewModel (View models). The validator follows the chain with the types it can see, starting at UUserWidget, and reports:

  • A warning for a segment the visible type lacks. The live object may be a subclass that has it, so the check stops there and the model can still resolve at run time. The SourcePath sample gets this warning on SampleViewModel: GetOwningPlayer returns APlayerController, which has no SampleViewModel, and the model resolves when the game runs.
  • An error for a segment that is not readable or not an object, and for a last type unrelated to the declared class.

A misspelled segment gets the same warning and never resolves, with no other message, so read the segment name in the warning.

items.title: View models
items.text:
A document reads data from Unreal MVVM view models (UMVVMViewModelBase) and calls their functions. Use one for anything a screen shows from your game or does to it. The head declares each model with <viewmodel> and the body reads it through data-model="<name>" (Concepts).

A declaration has a name, unique in the document, and a class, the path of a class that derives from UMVVMViewModelBase: /Script/<Module>.<Class> for a C++ class, or the generated class ..._C of a Blueprint (Blueprint view models). It also has exactly one source, the attribute that says where the instance comes from:

  • create: the document makes the instance.
  • context: the instance is looked up in the GameInstance's view model collection.
  • resolver: a resolver class makes the instance.
  • manual: game code assigns the instance.
  • path: the instance is read from a property or getter of the player controller, its pawn or the local player.

None or two is a head error. Two more attributes are optional:

  • optional: without it, focus entering the document's focus areas waits for an unresolved model; with it, focus does not wait, and validation reports a problem with the model's fields as a warning instead of an error. create cannot be combined with it.
  • settable: game code can replace the instance (Option: settable).

An attribute the declaration does not know is a warning, except on a resolver declaration, where it sets a property of the resolver.

Only Field Notify fields are read, and the document updates when the model broadcasts a change (Data binding). Which source fits which screen is a table in Designing a game's UI.

items.title: Source: create
items.text:
The document makes its own view model when it opens. The instance lives as long as the document's view: it is new after the document is closed and opened again, and a keep-alive document that is only parked keeps it. create cannot be combined with optional, and an abstract class is an error. This is the source of the FieldBinding, Events, Lists, StructList, NestedViewModel and Component samples:

FieldBinding.rml
<viewmodel name="fields" class="/Script/ArcRmlUISamples.ArcRmlSamplesFieldBindingViewModel" create="true"/>

A model that holds other view models makes them in its constructor with CreateDefaultSubobject (Data binding).

items.title: Source: context
items.text:
The view model is looked up in the GameInstance's MVVM view model collection by its class and a context name. Game code adds the instance before it opens the document, so the document shows it from the first frame. Sample: SourceContext.

SourceContext.rml
<viewmodel name="item" class="/Script/ArcRmlUISamples.ArcRmlSamplesSourceContextViewModel" context="VM_SampleContext"/>
C++Blueprint SourceContext/ArcRmlSamplesSourceContext.cpp
const FArcRmlDocumentRef Document{TEXT("/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/SourceContext/SourceContext.rml")};
UMVVMGameSubsystem* Mvvm = LocalPlayer->GetGameInstance()->GetSubsystem<UMVVMGameSubsystem>();
if (!Mvvm)
{
    return FArcRmlDocumentRef();
}

FMVVMViewModelContext Context;
Context.ContextClass = UArcRmlSamplesSourceContextViewModel::StaticClass();
Context.ContextName = TEXT("VM_SampleContext");
Mvvm->GetViewModelCollection()->RemoveViewModel(Context);
UArcRmlSamplesSourceContextViewModel* Instance = NewObject<UArcRmlSamplesSourceContextViewModel>(Mvvm);
Instance->Label = TEXT("From the GameInstance collection");
Mvvm->GetViewModelCollection()->AddViewModelInstance(Context, Instance);

return Viewport->OpenDocument(Document) ? Document : FArcRmlDocumentRef();

This is an excerpt from the body of the sample's Open function: LocalPlayer is its parameter and Viewport is the local player's UArcRmlViewportSubsystem, as in the Quick start.

BP_SourceContext_Open is a Blueprint Function Library. Its Open function (input PlayerController, output Document) runs:

  1. Make Arc Rml Document Ref with Path /ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/SourceContext/SourceContext.rml, and Arc Rml Viewport Subsystem (in the palette: Get ArcRmlViewportSubsystem) with the PlayerController input.
  2. Viewmodel Game Subsytem (the engine's own spelling of the node title) with WorldContext the PlayerController, then Get View Model Collection on it.
  3. Make MVVMView Model Context with ContextClass the view model class and ContextName VM_SampleContext, and Remove View Model on the collection with that context.
  4. Construct Arc Rml Samples Source Context View Model with the MVVM game subsystem as its outer, SET w/ Broadcast of Label on the instance, and Add View Model Instance on the collection with the context and the instance.
  5. Open Document on the viewport subsystem; when it returns true, the function returns the document.

While the instance is not in the collection the model is unresolved. The document retries every second and when the collection changes.

items.title: Source: resolver
items.text:
A resolver is a C++ class derived from UMVVMViewModelContextResolver that creates the instance. Every attribute of the declaration that is not one of the declaration's own is set on the resolver property of the same name before CreateInstance runs; a name the resolver does not have is a warning. The names name, class, context, resolver, create, manual, path, settable, optional, preview and on-close belong to the declaration, so a resolver property cannot have one of them. CreateInstance receives a widget owned by the local player, so a resolver can read the player. Sample: SourceResolver; the Greeting attribute fills the resolver's Greeting property.

SourceResolver.rml
<viewmodel name="greeting" class="/Script/ArcRmlUISamples.ArcRmlSamplesSourceResolverViewModel" resolver="/Script/ArcRmlUISamples.ArcRmlSamplesGreetingResolver" Greeting="Hello from the RML attribute"/>
SourceResolver/ArcRmlSamplesSourceResolver.h
UCLASS()
class UArcRmlSamplesGreetingResolver : public UMVVMViewModelContextResolver
{
    GENERATED_BODY()

public:
    UPROPERTY(EditAnywhere, Category = "Samples")
    FString Greeting;

    virtual UObject* CreateInstance(const UClass* ExpectedType, const UUserWidget* UserWidget, const UMVVMView* View) const override;
};
SourceResolver/ArcRmlSamplesSourceResolver.cpp
UObject* UArcRmlSamplesGreetingResolver::CreateInstance(const UClass* ExpectedType, const UUserWidget* UserWidget, const UMVVMView* View) const
{
    if (ExpectedType && !UArcRmlSamplesSourceResolverViewModel::StaticClass()->IsChildOf(ExpectedType))
    {
        return nullptr;
    }

    UArcRmlSamplesSourceResolverViewModel* ViewModel = NewObject<UArcRmlSamplesSourceResolverViewModel>(GetTransientPackage());
    ViewModel->Greeting = Greeting;
    const APlayerController* Player = UserWidget ? UserWidget->GetOwningPlayer() : nullptr;
    ViewModel->PlayerName = Player ? Player->GetName() : FString(TEXT("no player"));
    return ViewModel;
}

items.title: Source: manual
items.text:
A manual declaration creates nothing: the model stays unresolved until game code assigns an object with SetViewModel. manual implies settable and optional. Sample: SourceManual.

SourceManual.rml
<viewmodel name="item" class="/Script/ArcRmlUISamples.ArcRmlSamplesSourceManualViewModel" manual="true"/>
C++Blueprint SourceManual/ArcRmlSamplesSourceManual.cpp
const FArcRmlDocumentRef Document{TEXT("/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/SourceManual/SourceManual.rml")};
UArcRmlSamplesSourceManualViewModel* First = NewObject<UArcRmlSamplesSourceManualViewModel>(GetTransientPackage());
First->Label = TEXT("Instance 1");
if (!Viewport->SetViewModel(Document, TEXT("item"), First))
{
    return FArcRmlDocumentRef();
}

return Viewport->OpenDocument(Document) ? Document : FArcRmlDocumentRef();

This is an excerpt from the body of the sample's Open function; Viewport is the local player's UArcRmlViewportSubsystem.

BP_SourceManual_Open is a Blueprint Function Library. Its Open function (input PlayerController, output Document) runs:

  1. Make Arc Rml Document Ref with Path /ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/SourceManual/SourceManual.rml, and Arc Rml Viewport Subsystem with the PlayerController input.
  2. Construct Arc Rml Samples Source Manual View Model with the PlayerController as its outer, and SET w/ Broadcast of Label on the instance with Instance 1.
  3. Set View Model on the viewport subsystem with the document, ModelName item and the instance.
  4. When Set View Model returns true, Open Document; when that returns true, the function returns the document.

The document shows Waiting for the view model (its !ArcResolved branch) until the first assignment. The "Swap the instance" button calls Swap, which makes a new view model and assigns it while the document is open:

SourceManual/ArcRmlSamplesSourceManual.cpp
void UArcRmlSamplesSourceManualViewModel::Swap(UObject* WorldContextObject)
{
    UArcRmlViewportSubsystem* Viewport = ArcRmlSamplesSourceManualPrivate::FindViewport(WorldContextObject);
    if (!Viewport)
    {
        return;
    }

    UArcRmlSamplesSourceManualViewModel* Next = NewObject<UArcRmlSamplesSourceManualViewModel>(GetTransientPackage());
    Next->Generation = Generation + 1;
    Next->Label = FString::Printf(TEXT("Instance %d"), Next->Generation);
    Viewport->SetViewModel(FArcRmlDocumentRef{TEXT("/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/SourceManual/SourceManual.rml")}, TEXT("item"), Next);
}

Swap takes a parameter named WorldContextObject, which the call fills with the local player controller (Events); that is how the function reaches the player's subsystem.

items.title: Source: path
items.text:
The view model is read from an object property chain, starting at a widget the plugin creates for the player controller. The roots are the UUserWidget getters GetOwningPlayer, GetOwningPlayerPawn and GetOwningLocalPlayer. A segment is a Blueprint-visible object property or a const, zero-argument BlueprintCallable function that returns an object. Each segment is looked up on the class of the live object, so a member of your own player controller or pawn class is found without a cast. The result must be the declared class or a subclass. A path needs a player; a null on the way leaves the model unresolved and the document evaluates the path again later. Sample: SourcePath.

SourcePath.rml
<viewmodel name="item" class="/Script/ArcRmlUISamples.ArcRmlSamplesSourcePathViewModel" path="GetOwningPlayer.SampleViewModel"/>

SampleViewModel is a property of the sample's AArcRmlSamplesPlayerController, declared in ArcRmlSamplesGameMode.h and made in ArcRmlSamplesGameMode.cpp:

ArcRmlSamplesGameMode.h
UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, Category = "Samples")
TObjectPtr<UArcRmlSamplesSourcePathViewModel> SampleViewModel;
ArcRmlSamplesGameMode.cpp
SampleViewModel = CreateDefaultSubobject<UArcRmlSamplesSourcePathViewModel>(TEXT("SampleViewModel"));

The validator warns on this path

Validation reports a view-model-path warning on SampleViewModel, because it cannot see your own controller or pawn class. The path works at run time. Any path into a member of your own class gets this warning. A misspelled segment gets the same warning and never resolves, with no other message, so check the spelling when you see it. An unreadable or non-object segment, and a path whose result type is unrelated to the declared class, are view-model-path errors.

items.title: Option: settable
items.text:
settable="true" lets game code replace the instance of a model whatever its source. In the SourceSettable sample the first object comes from the context collection and the "Replace the instance" button swaps it:

SourceSettable.rml
<viewmodel name="item" class="/Script/ArcRmlUISamples.ArcRmlSamplesSourceSettableViewModel" context="VM_SampleSettable" settable="true"/>
SourceSettable/ArcRmlSamplesSourceSettable.cpp
void UArcRmlSamplesSourceSettableViewModel::Replace(UObject* WorldContextObject)
{
    UArcRmlViewportSubsystem* Viewport = ArcRmlSamplesSourceSettablePrivate::FindViewport(WorldContextObject);
    if (!Viewport)
    {
        return;
    }

    UArcRmlSamplesSourceSettableViewModel* Next = NewObject<UArcRmlSamplesSourceSettableViewModel>(GetTransientPackage());
    Next->Generation = Generation + 1;
    Next->Label = FString::Printf(TEXT("Replacement %d"), Next->Generation);
    Viewport->SetViewModel(FArcRmlDocumentRef{TEXT("/ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/SourceSettable/SourceSettable.rml")}, TEXT("item"), Next);
}

A model that was set by hand is skipped by the retry and by collection changes. SetViewModel with nullptr removes the assignment and sends the model back to its own source, here the collection.

items.title: Option: on-close
items.text:
on-close="<function>" names a function of the model that takes no arguments. The plugin calls it when the document closes or is parked (keep-alive, Documents), once per close or park. A parked document that is later destroyed calls nothing, and neither does a model that never resolved. In a frame, a tab's on-close also runs when a tab switch hides that tab. Use it to release or answer something the open document held. The demo's dialog model is manual, and Closed runs the pending callback with the cancel index when the host closes the dialog:

Dialog.rml
<viewmodel name="dialog" class="/Script/ArcRmlUIDemo.ArcRmlDemoDialogViewModel" manual on-close="Closed"/>
ArcRmlDemoDialogViewModel.cpp
void UArcRmlDemoDialogViewModel::Closed()
{
    if (const TFunction<void(int32)> Callback = TakeCallback())
    {
        Callback(CancelIndex);
    }
}

The validator checks that the function exists and takes no arguments.

items.title: SetViewModel
items.text:
SetViewModel(Document, ModelName, ViewModel) is a function of UArcRmlViewportSubsystem, in C++ and Blueprint, and returns whether it took the object.

  • It reads the head of the named document, so the document need not be open. It returns false, with a warning in the log, for a document whose head cannot be read, a name with no <viewmodel>, a declaration that is neither manual nor settable, and an object that is not of the declared class.
  • The assignment is kept per document. A set before OpenDocument shows from the first frame; a set after the open replaces the object and updates every binding.
  • nullptr removes the assignment and the model returns to its own source: a new instance for create, the property chain for path, the collection for context, the resolver for resolver, unresolved for manual. On a model with no assignment it does nothing.
  • The assignment is kept until the document closes. A parked keep-alive document keeps it.
  • SetViewModelByClass(Document, ViewModel) sets the one manual or settable declaration of the document whose class the object is, and returns false when there are none or two.
  • GetViewModel(Document, ModelName) returns the live object of an open document, whatever its source, and null when the document is parked or closed.

items.title: Fields every model gets
items.text:
These names are reserved: a view model field with one of them is not bound and logs an error.

  • ArcResolved is true once the view model exists. An unresolved model still binds, from the class defaults, so give the document a fallback. The sample documents show the pattern: <div data-if="ArcResolved">...</div> and <span data-if="!ArcResolved">Waiting for the view model</span>.
  • ArcEmpty is an empty array, which a component prop with a [] default receives.
  • ArcKeys holds key labels as text for the current input device: ArcKeys.<Action> for each action of the document's input-mapping context, by the action's asset name, and confirm, back, navigate, stepLeft, stepRight and scheme (keyboard or gamepad). The GamepadMenu sample shows them as prompts:
GamepadMenu.rml
<span class="gm-prompt">{{ ArcKeys.confirm }} Select</span>
<span id="gm-info" class="gm-prompt" data-hotkey="IA_Sample_MenuInfo" data-event-click="call('', 'ToggleInfo')">{{ ArcKeys.IA_Sample_MenuInfo }} Info</span>
<span class="gm-prompt">{{ ArcKeys.back }} Close</span>

These are three lines of the sample's <body>.

A document with no <viewmodel> that reads ArcKeys gets a model named ArcDocument on its <body>; it has ArcResolved (true) and ArcKeys. Input and gamepad covers the keys.
