items.title: Walkthrough: the SaveLoad screen
items.text:
The companion plugin ArcRmlUIDemo is a complete game UI built on ArcRmlUI. This page reads one of its screens, Save / Load, from top to bottom: a slot list with an empty state, a detail panel, a sort dropdown, a delete confirm, prompts that follow the focus, one hotkey and Back. Each part links the page that explains the feature. The excerpts are copied from /ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/SaveLoad.rml and the screen's view model, Source/ArcRmlUIDemo/ArcRmlDemoSaveLoadViewModel.h / .cpp. Read it after the feature pages to see them combined in one real screen. The excerpts are shortened to the lines that matter.

Demo code and plugin API

The RML attributes, <viewmodel> declarations, dc-import, ArcKeys and data-focus-active on this page are ArcRmlUI. Everything in the ArcRmlUIDemo module is demo code that you write differently in your game: the ARC_RML_DEMO_SET macro, the demo subsystem UArcRmlDemoSubsystem that opens and closes the screens, the view model base classes, the resolver ArcRmlDemoViewModelResolver, the components under /ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/ and the gu-* classes of GameUI.rcss.

items.title: Run the demo
items.text: Put the ArcRmlUIDemo folder in your project's Plugins folder (its README.md lists the setup), open the map /ArcRmlUIDemo/Demo/Maps/L_ArcRmlDemo and press Play. The map's game mode starts the demo; outside Shipping builds, ArcRmlDemo.Start in the console starts it in any map with a local player. Load Game in the main menu opens the screen in load mode, Save Game in the pause menu in save mode.

items.title: The head
Two view models
items.text:
The head declares two models, and the body reads each through its own data-model:

SaveLoad.rml
<body data-model="ui"
    data-class-theme-ember="Theme == 'ember'"
    data-class-theme-daylight="Theme == 'daylight'"
    data-event-back="call('', 'Back'); stopPropagation()"
    data-event-uiaction="callIf(ev.action == 'IA_ArcDemo_DevBar', '', 'ToggleDevBar')">
    <div class="gu-layer">
        <div class="gu-screen" data-model="saveload">
  • ui is shared by every demo screen: the theme and the dev bar. Its source is context, so it is looked up in the GameInstance's view model collection, where the demo adds it when it starts (Source: context). The data-class-theme-* bindings on <body> read its Theme (Themes).
  • saveload is this screen's own state. Its source is a resolver (Source: resolver); the demo's resolver returns one instance per class and player, so the state survives closing and opening the screen.
  • ev.action in the data-event-uiaction line is the name of the Input Action that fired (UI actions); here IA_ArcDemo_DevBar (F10) calls ToggleDevBar.
  • Both classes are Blueprint children of C++ view models; the Blueprints hold the data defaults (Blueprint view models).

call('', ...) calls the model of the element's nearest data-model (Calls): inside gu-screen that is saveload, on <body> it is ui.

items.title: The list and its empty state
items.text:
SaveLoad.rml
<div class="sl-grid" data-if="Slots.size > 0" data-focus-area="slots" data-focus-primary="">
    <dc-import name="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/SaveSlotCard"
        data-for="slSlot, slSlot_index : Slots"
        state="{{ slSlot.State }}"
        slot-label="{{ slSlot.SlotLabel }}"
        title="{{ slSlot.Title }}"
        location="{{ slSlot.Location }}"
        playtime="{{ slSlot.Playtime }}"
        date="{{ slSlot.Date }}"
        autosave-label="Auto"
        empty-label="Empty slot"
        empty-hint="{{ slSlot.EmptyHint }}"
        corrupted-label="Data corrupted"
        corrupted-hint="This file cannot be read."
        selected="{{ slSlot_index == SelectedSlot }}"
        focusable="{{ true }}"
        autofocus="{{ slSlot_index == SelectedSlot }}"
        data-event-click="call('', 'Activate', slSlot_index)"
        style="width: 100%"/>
</div>
<dc-import name="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/EmptyState"
    data-if="Slots.size == 0"
    icon="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/icons/folder-x.svg"
    title="No saved games"
    body="Your saves and autosaves will appear here."
    style="width: 100%">
    <dc-import name="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/Button"
        label="New game"
        icon-left="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/icons/plus.svg"/>
</dc-import>
  • data-if shows the grid while Slots has rows and the empty state when it has none; .size is the array's length (Fields).
  • data-for="slSlot, slSlot_index : Slots" on the import makes one card per row, with the row and its index (Lists). The click passes the index to Activate.
  • selected and autofocus compare the index with SelectedSlot, so focus lands on the selected slot when the area is entered, also after the screen is opened again. No view model field follows the focus.
ArcRmlDemoSaveLoadViewModel.h
UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, FieldNotify, Category = "ArcRmlDemo")
TArray<FArcRmlDemoSaveSlotRow> Slots;

UPROPERTY(BlueprintReadOnly, FieldNotify, Category = "ArcRmlDemo")
int32 SelectedSlot = 1;

Slots is a TArray of a row struct. The view model rebuilds it from the demo's game model, so a save or a delete changes the list.

items.title: Components and slots
items.text:
Every dc-import above expands a component by its package path, with props as attributes and {{ }} values bound to the screen's model (Props). Children of an import fill its slots (Slots):

  • the "New game" button sits in the default slot of EmptyState;
  • the sort dropdown sits in the default slot of SectionHeader (below);
  • the action buttons sit in the footer slot of Panel, whose import sets has-footer="{{ true }}" because the panel shows its footer only with that prop:
SaveLoad.rml
<div slot="footer" class="sl-actions" data-focus-area="actions" data-focus-parent="slots">
    <dc-import name="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/Button"
        label="Delete"
        variant="ghost"
        icon-left="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/icons/trash-2.svg"
        disabled="{{ bNoDelete }}"
        focusable="{{ true }}"
        data-focus-enter="modal"
        data-event-click="callIf(!bNoDelete, '', 'Delete')"/>

Delete is reachable while disabled: disabled only changes its look, so the click is guarded with callIf(!bNoDelete, ...) (callIf).

items.title: Focus areas
items.text:
The screen has four areas (Focus areas):

Area Element Attributes slots the slot grid data-focus-primary sort the sort dropdown none actions the panel footer data-focus-parent="slots" modal the delete confirm data-focus-contain SaveLoad.rml
<div class="sl-sort" data-focus-area="sort">
    <dc-import name="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/Dropdown"
        data-focus-owner=""
        value="Most recent"
        field="sort"
        style="width: 100%"/>
</div>
  • slots is the primary area, so the screen opens on the grid, at the autofocus card.
  • Arrows leave an area at its edge to the nearest item of another area (Leaving an area).
  • Back in actions returns to its parent slots (Back and the parent area), and a leave from a slot into actions records that slot as the area's origin. The other areas have no parent, so their Back goes to <body> (Back).

The confirm is an area inside the screen, shown while bConfirm is true:

SaveLoad.rml
<div class="gu-area" data-if="bConfirm" data-focus-area="modal" data-focus-contain="">
    <dc-import name="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/Modal"
        backdrop="{{ true }}"
        variant="danger"
        title="Delete this save?"
        body="{{ ConfirmBody }}"
        buttons="{{ ConfirmButtons }}"
        focused="{{ 0 }}"/>
</div>
  • data-focus-contain: the arrows never leave the confirm (Containing focus).
  • The Delete button and both Delete prompts carry data-focus-enter="modal". After their click, focus enters modal once Delete has run and the area is shown, and lands on the button that Modal's focused prop marks autofocus (Cancel).
  • The confirm's buttons call Choose(index) on saveload: 0 is Cancel, 1 deletes the slot.
ArcRmlDemoSaveLoadViewModel.cpp
void UArcRmlDemoSaveLoadViewModel::Delete()
{
    if (bConfirm || !GetSlots().IsValidIndex(SelectedSlot) || GetSlots()[SelectedSlot].State == TEXT("empty"))
    {
        return;
    }
    ARC_RML_DEMO_SET(*this, bConfirm, true);
    Refresh();
}

Limits

  • data-focus-enter is read only from a click (a mouse click, pad accept, a hotkey or cycle step), never from a key handler that calls the view model.
  • A data-if that turns true builds its branch again, so focus, scroll and hover state inside it start fresh (Limits).
  • A custom element that looks disabled stays a focus stop; only a disabled form control loses it.

items.title: Prompts per area
items.text:
The footer holds one prompt group per area, and GameUI.rcss shows the group of the active area. The plugin sets data-focus-active on <body> to the name of the area that holds the focus, so CSS can switch groups without a view model field:

SaveLoad.rml
<div class="gu-prompts gu-default" data-area="slots" data-if="!bConfirm">
    <dc-import name="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/PromptBar">
        <dc-import name="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/InputPrompt"
            key-label="{{ ArcKeys.confirm }}"
            label="{{ Mode == 'save' ? 'Save' : 'Load' }}"
            disabled="{{ bNoPrimary }}"/>
        <dc-import name="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/InputPrompt"
            key-label="{{ ArcKeys.IA_ArcDemo_Delete }}"
            label="Delete"
            disabled="{{ bNoDelete }}"
            data-hotkey="IA_ArcDemo_Delete"
            data-focus-enter="modal"
            data-event-click="callIf(!bNoDelete, '', 'Delete')"/>
        <dc-import name="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/InputPrompt"
            key-label="{{ ArcKeys.back }}"
            label="Back"/>
    </dc-import>
</div>
GameUI.rcss
.gu-prompts {
    display: none;
}

.gu-prompts.gu-all,
body:not([data-focus-active]) .gu-prompts.gu-default,
/* the full sheet repeats this selector for every focus area name used by any demo screen */
body[data-focus-active="slots"] .gu-prompts[data-area="slots"] {
    display: contents;
}

The full sheet repeats this selector for every focus area name used by any demo screen. gu-default also shows while no area is active, and gu-all always. A data-if on bConfirm replaces the groups with Confirm and Cancel while the confirm is open:

SaveLoad.rml
<div class="gu-prompts gu-all" data-if="bConfirm">
    <dc-import name="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/PromptBar">
        <dc-import name="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/InputPrompt"
            key-label="{{ ArcKeys.confirm }}"
            label="Confirm"/>
        <dc-import name="/ArcRmlUIDemo/UI/Rml/Demo/Components/InputPrompt"
            key-label="{{ ArcKeys.back }}"
            label="Cancel"/>
    </dc-import>
</div>

The key labels are ArcKeys: confirm and back for the project's Confirm and Back, IA_ArcDemo_Delete for the screen's action, each for the current input device (Fields every model gets).

items.title: The hotkey
items.text:
The Delete prompts carry data-hotkey="IA_ArcDemo_Delete": when that action fires, the prompt is clicked, so its data-event-click and data-focus-enter run as for the button (The menu's own action). A hotkey clicks only a visible element, so the key works exactly while a Delete prompt is shown: in slots and actions, not in sort or while the confirm is open.

Limits

When several visible elements carry the same hotkey, the one on the focus chain is clicked, else the first visible one in the focused area, then in the document; nothing is reported. Here two prompt groups carry the Delete hotkey, and CSS shows one at a time.

items.title: Back
items.text:
One handler on <body> handles Back for the whole screen (Back): the data-event-back attribute of the <body> shown in Two view models, call('', 'Back'); stopPropagation().

Back in actions first returns focus to its parent slots, on the slot it was entered from, and never reaches <body> (Back and the parent area). With no saves there is no slots area, so that Back goes on to <body> like a Back in slots, sort or modal. <body> calls ui's Back and stops the event (stopPropagation), so the host never closes the document by itself on this screen. The demo's ui model passes Back to the model of the screen on top, here saveload:

ArcRmlDemoSaveLoadViewModel.cpp
void UArcRmlDemoSaveLoadViewModel::Back()
{
    if (bConfirm)
    {
        Choose(0);
        return;
    }
    Super::Back();
}

With the confirm open, Back cancels it. Otherwise the base class asks the demo subsystem to leave the screen, which closes the document and shows the screen below. The breadcrumb at the top of the screen (a row of screen names) also calls Back when you click its first name with the mouse; it is nofocus, so it is not a focus stop.

items.title: Working with documents
items.text: The loop a designer repeats: edit a document, see it change, check it. The editor reloads open documents on save, so no restart or reopen is needed.

items.title: Edit and save
items.text:
Edit the .rml and .rcss files in any text editor (the editor preview's Open in text editor opens one) and save. The editor watches the Content folder of every content root. About 0.2 seconds after the last change it compiles the changed .rml and .rcss files and reloads every open document, in the editor preview and in a game running in the editor. A changed .ttf, .otf, .svg, .png or .json file reloads them the same way.

A reload closes each open document and opens it again on its layer. What you see:

  • Lost: the text in fields, the scroll position and other state of the page, and the state kept by keep-alive documents (Keep-alive and preload).
  • Reset: the values of a view model that the document's head creates (create).
  • Kept: a view model that game code assigned with SetViewModel.
  • On an error: a document that fails to compile or read stays as it was, with the rest of its layer. The error shows as described below.

You should see the open document redraw with your change shortly after you save.

items.title: The preview
items.text: Editor preview shows a document without a game. Its Reload button compiles the document again and reloads the open documents, and Variant switches between the base data and the variants of the document's preview JSON. Changes made in its Bindings panel reload only the documents that read that preview file.

items.title: In a game
items.text:
These console commands exist in every build, except ArcRml.Inspect, which exists outside Shipping builds:

Command What it does ArcRml.Open <Path> Opens the document on its layer for the first local player. ArcRml.Close <Path> Closes the open document with that path. ArcRml.Preview <Path> [Variant] Opens the document with its preview data, or a variant of it; reopens it when it is open. ArcRml.Inspect [Path] Toggles the inspector for an open document: pick elements in the view, read them in a panel (Debugging layout). Without a path it closes the inspector.

<Path> is the package path, such as /ArcRmlUISamples/UI/Rml/FirstScreen/FirstScreen.rml.

items.title: Check a document
items.text: Run Validate RML on the changed files; it reports what compiling alone does not. Validation has the Content Browser entry, the console command and the command line run.

items.title: Where errors show
items.text:
• The editor's Message Log window, ArcRmlUI log: a compile that reports diagnostics for a changed file adds a page with them, and the page Validate holds the validator's result.
  • The preview's Diagnostics panel: the errors and warnings of the open document.
  • In a game outside Shipping, a bar over the viewport lists the errors and warnings of the open documents, and the same lines go to the log category LogArcRmlUI.

items.title: Next
items.text:

  • Debugging layout: pick elements in the view and read them in a panel.
  • Documents: the head, layers and how a document opens and closes.

items.title: World markers
items.text:
Use data-world for a label, health bar or quest marker that must stay over a point in the level while the camera moves.

The WorldMarker sample has a label that stays over a cube in the level. "Move" moves the cube sideways and the label follows it; a second "Move" moves it back. Run it with ArcRmlSamples.Open WorldMarker in the map L_ArcRmlSamples (Samples).

items.title: data-world
items.text:
data-world="Expr" places an element over a point in the world. The value is a string of three numbers separated by whitespace, "x y z" in centimetres. The document sets the element's transform to a translate to the point's place on the screen each time the point or the camera changes.

WorldMarker.rml
<body data-model="marker">
    <div id="wm-marker" class="wm-marker" data-world="Anchor">
        <div class="wm-label">Target</div>
    </div>
WorldMarker.rcss
.wm-marker {
    position: absolute;
    left: 0;
    top: 0;
}

.wm-label {
    transform: translate(-50%, -100%);
}

Limits

  • The anchored element needs position: absolute; left: 0; top: 0: the translate starts from the element's own layout position, so that position must be the top-left corner of the screen.
  • The element's own transform is overwritten by data-world. An offset of your own goes on a child: translate(-50%, -100%) on .wm-label centres the label over the point and puts it above.
  • data-world needs a data-model on the element or an ancestor, like every data attribute; without one it does nothing.
  • The element is hidden before its first UI update, while the point is behind the camera, and while the view has no camera.

items.title: The value
items.text:
The sample's view model keeps Anchor as a string and refreshes it every frame while the document is open.

WorldMarker/ArcRmlSamplesWorldMarker.cpp
bool UArcRmlSamplesWorldMarkerViewModel::UpdateAnchor(float DeltaTime)
{
    if (const AActor* Actor = Target.Get())
    {
        const FVector Location = Actor->GetActorLocation();
        UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE(Anchor, FString::Printf(TEXT("%.1f %.1f %.1f"), Location.X, Location.Y, Location.Z));
    }
    return true;
}

The sample's Open function finds the cube by its actor tag SampleMarkerTarget and hands it to the view model, which updates Anchor on a ticker while the document is open. UE_MVVM_SET_PROPERTY_VALUE sends the value only when it changed.

  • An empty or whitespace-only value hides the element without an error, so the label stays hidden until your code first sets Anchor. To hide it again when the target is gone, set an empty string; the sample does not, so its label stays at the last point.
  • Any other value that is not three finite numbers hides the element and logs one error per view: data-world on element <address>: '<text>' is not a world point "x y z".
  • The camera is the one of the owning local player.
